item.title: Red Sox's Triston Casas Hits Home Run In First At-Bat In 574 Days
item.description: Boston Red Sox first baseman Triston Casas The Major League Baseball Season may be over, but baseball is still happening around the world. The Dominican Winter League is one of the premier winter leagues, and this year, Triston Casas is playing for the Tigres Del Licey. On Friday night, he played in his first game of the season and hit a grand slam in the bottom of the first inning. TRISTON CASAS GRAND SLAM IN HIS FIRST LIDOM PA SINCE OCT 2022 pic.twitter.com/tNNrDspcHB — Sarah Langs (@SlangsOnSports) November 28, 2026 It was Casas' first at-bat in any league since May 2, 2025, 574 days ago. This is Casas' second time suiting up for the Tigres Del Licey. The first stint he had in the Dominican Winter League came in 2022. His grand slam was his lone hit of the game, but it is a potential sign of what's to come when he's back in the big leagues. Casas was great in the only big league season in which he played over 130 games. In 2023, he slashed .263/.367/.490 with 24 home runs. However, he has battled injuries ever since. In 2024, he missed 99 games with torn cartilage in his rib cage, but still hit 13 home runs with a .800 OPS in 63 games. In 2025, he got off to a slow start and then ruptured his left patellar tendon. He missed the rest of the year, suffered setbacks this year, and missed all of the 2026 season. This year, he dealt with an abdominal strain and underwent wrist surgery. Things are different now for the Red Sox than they were the last time Casas played. They have a new starting first baseman, and with Jake Bauers also on the team, Casas may not even be the backup. At-bats will be hard to come by for him, and he could be traded. item.title: Kentucky basketball’s illegal in-bounds play has fans creating Mark Pope replacement lists
item.description: (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Mark Pope entered the year with Kentucky men’s basketball desperately needing a signature season and a deep NCAA tournament run to save his job and regain the momentum of the program. Instead, Pope’s Wildcats are already in danger of missing March Madness less than a month into the 2026-27 campaign after suffering their third embarrassing loss so far on Friday night. Wichita State beat Kentucky, 73-71 in overtime, on a loss that can be blamed directly on coaching. Kentucky already got destroyed by Kansas in the Champions Classic, then lost handily to a good-not-great Indiana team. This Wichita State loss feels like the new low point of the Pope era, not because the Shockers are bad — they’re now ranked nine spots ahead of Kentucky on KenPom — but because of how the Wildcats lost. Pope was booed off the floor at home as he walked off the court after the loss to Wichita State. He deserved it for how poorly he managed the end of the game. Kentucky should have had one last chance to tie or win the game down two with 5.4 seconds remaining in overtime. Pope went into the huddle and drew up a play that directly resulted in a turnover. The Wildcats tried to get tricky inbounding the ball under their own basket, but Pope’s play was illegal for passing the ball across the baseline. This is as humiliating as it gets for a coach already under fire. Kentucky inbound turnover pic.twitter.com/ryIWoB4QPo — wok (@wokdior) November 28, 2026 Pope took full accountability for the play after the game. “That’s 100% on me, guys. That is 100% me. Somehow that changed to a live ball in my mind and I messed that up. And it’s really costly. It’s a tough one to carry as a coach, for sure. Kentucky’s final play wasn’t their only miscue. Down two with 35 seconds left, Pope drew up a play for his $6 million man Milan Momcilovic , who promptly stepped out of bounds. Watch the play here: Milan Momcilovic steps out of bounds wow pic.twitter.com/SjqzMju5dN — wok (@wokdior) November 28, 2026 Kentucky actually did get one more chance to win the game after the illegal play on the baseline. Wichita State turned the ball over on the next possession, and Momcilovic got a decent look at a game-winning three, but missed. What this comes down to is poor execution by Kentucky, and it has Big Blue Nation ready to move on. Pope heard some boos from the home fans as he walked off the floor after the game: Mark Pope Boo’d out of Rupp Arena pic.twitter.com/C4n2tEvQ0z — Bleed Blue Network (@BleedBNetwork) November 28, 2026 Kentucky fell to No. 66 on KenPom after the loss . Teams usually need to be in the top-40 or top-45 to get an at-large bid to March Madness, and their level of play this season won’t even be good enough for the expanded 76-team field . The Cats are now considered an underdog in almost every SEC game the rest of the year by the computer metrics. Kentucky fans are already putting out their list of coaches to replace Pope. This

item.title: Antonelli leads Mercedes one-two in final practice for F1 Qatar GP
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Italian Formula One driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli of team Mercedes drives during the second practice of the Formula 1 2026 Qatar Grand Prix, at Lusail International Circuit. (is associated with: «Antonelli leads Mercedes one-two in final practice for F1 Qatar GP») Alessio Morgese/ZUMA Press Wire/dpa World champion Kimi Antonelli led a third Mercedes one-two ahead of team-mate George Russell in the final practice for the Formula One Qatar Grand Prix on Saturday. The top two was a repetition of the previous two practice sessions on Friday. The Italian clocked the fastest time of 1 minute 22.400 seconds, beating Russell by 0.249 seconds. Max Verstappen of Red Bull was third ahead of team-mate Isack Hadjar. Charles Leclerc of Ferrari was fifth, with the McLaren duo of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri right behind in sixth and seventh respectively. Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton was ninth in the other Ferrari. The race in Qatar is taking place despite continuing security concerns due to conflicts in the Middle East. Several broadcasters and other personnel decided against attending the penultimate race of the season. Williams driver Carlos Sainz, who was 18th in practice, revealed on Thursday that drivers were briefed on emergency evacuation procedures and was surprised to discover journalists knew nothing about it. "I was told there was such a plan, and I expected the press would be included, too," he said. Qualifying for Sunday's showdown is later on Saturday. There's nothing more at stake at this point of the year, as Antonelli has already clinched the drivers' title and Mercedes have claimed the constructors' championship.

item.title: INEC Mock Election Scorecard: Low turnouts, poor awareness, BVAS glitches mar exercise
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, organised mocked polls across the country today with mixed results and turnouts. The exercise was to test INEC’s preparedness for the 2027 elections, expecially the technical aspects. However, despite reports of poor numbers, the INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, expressed satisfaction with the conduct of the nationwide mock accreditation exercise. He assured Nigerians of the commission’s readiness to deliver credible elections in 2027. Amupitan, who visited Jos on Saturday to monitor the exercise, inspected polling locations, including Obasanjo Model School in Jos South Local Government Area, where he observed voter accreditation and the performance of electoral technology. Speaking to journalists, the INEC chairman described the turnout and conduct of the exercise as impressive. “You can see yourself that it is very impressive. The turnout is very good,” he said. Uploaded results Meanwhile, about 1,995 results (approximately 12%) of the 17,614 expected, had been uploaded as of 3:09 pm on Saturday in the nationwide INEC mock presidential election. The Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise, which started at 8:30a.m., ended at 2:30pm. However, more than 30 minutes later, the portal puts the “Percentage uploaded” at 11.33 per cent. Its last recorded upload came at 3:09:11 pm from polling unit 32/04/05/005, at press time. Low turnout in Lagos Low turnout of eligible voters marred the mock accreditation exercise conducted in parts of Lagos State, with some voters blaming the commission’s inadequate publicity. Polling agents expressed concern over the poor participation when Vanguard visited some of the designated polling units in Ijegun, Satellite Town and Festac, in the Amuwo-Odofin area of the state. An INEC polling agent at one of the polling units said only about 40 of the 250 registered voters had participated in the exercise as of the time of the visit. …in Katsina, too; poor publicity Also, low voter turnout and inadequate public awareness characterised the mock accreditation exercise conducted by lNEC in Katsina State on Saturday, ahead of the 2027 general elections. Vanguard monitoring of the exercise at Star Election Polling Unit, Wakilin Kudu 1, Kofar Gidan Iro Isansi, Rafin Dadi, showed that only a few voters turned out to participate, although some were successfully accredited. The low participation raised concerns about the level of public sensitisation and awareness among eligible voters regarding the importance of the exercise. Apathy in Abia In Abia Stste, voter apathy marred the mock accreditation and result-upload exercise conducted by INEC, with several polling units recording zero or minimal turnout. At St. Stephen’s Primary School, Umuahia, some residents who turned out expressed disappointment that the exercise was restricted to selected polling units, blaming inadequate publicity for the low participation. item.title: Steelers WR DK Metcalf fined by NFL
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 22: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson #14 and referees attempt to keep Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf #4 from lunging at Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean #33 during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Pittsburg Steelers on November 22nd, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers rallied the troops and dominated the AFC West-leading Denver Broncos on Black Friday in Acrisure Stadium, 27-5. However, less than 24 hours after the win, the Steelers’ top receiver is back in the headlines after being fined by the NFL for his actions during the team’s Week 11 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles. Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reported on Saturday that the league has fined Metcalf a total of $26,867 for several infractions that occurred during the Steelers’ Week 11 game. The receiver was ejected from the Steelers game against the Eagles after receiving his second personal foul of the game for an altercation with Philadelphia defensive back Cooper DeJean. It looked as though Metcalf was trying to poke the eyes of the defensive back, but the receiver has denied those allegations. Although Metcalf has not been clear about what exactly transpired on the field, it landed him in the headlines for all the wrong reasons. The game marked the third ejection in the career of Metcalf, his first since 2023 and his first as a Steeler. Some expected Metcalf to receive a suspension from the league office for the repeat offense, but the league said he would not be suspended and could still face fines. The large fine we see today will be the only punishment Metcalf faces for his Week 11 actions. The receiver made his mark yesterday with a spectacular touchdown catch on Broncos standout cornerback Patrick Surtain in the Steelers’ dominant win and used sign language to say, “keep standing on business 4.” Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! item.title: Why Texas won’t beat Georgia in SEC Championship game
item.description: © Sara Diggins/American-Statesman / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Why Texas won’t beat Georgia in SEC Championship game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Georgia Bulldogs will beat the Texas Longhorns in the SEC Championship Game because their defense can dictate what Arch Manning faces on third down. Texas clinched its berth with a 16-6 road win over the Texas A&M Aggies. The Longhorns’ defense carried them in College Station, where their offense scored just one touchdown. Georgia was No. 1 and Texas was No. 3 in the Week 13 College Football Playoff rankings. They clash Saturday, December 5, at 4 p.m. ET on ABC at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta. The Bulldogs have won the past two SEC titles and all three meetings since the Longhorns joined the SEC. Georgia can put Texas behind schedule Texas totaled 83 net rushing yards across the three losses to Georgia. The Longhorns managed 29 in Austin in October 2024, 31 in that December’s overtime SEC Championship Game and 23 in Athens in November 2025. In the most recent meeting, Texas went 2-for-12 on third down in a 35-10 loss. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The current numbers give Georgia a chance to impose the same terms. Texas averaged 3.5 yards per carry in the regular season and managed 99 yards on 34 attempts in their Week 13 rivalry matchup with Texas A&M. Georgia allowed 2.9 yards per carry through 11 games entering their matchup vs. the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets. A short gain on first down gives Georgia more freedom to rush on third down, when Manning has fewer ways to keep the defense guessing. Texas gave up 35 sacks in 12 games. If the Longhorns spend the afternoon needing seven or eight yards on third down, they will ask their protection to hold up while receivers work deeper. Manning can make those throws. Sustaining drives that way is a much harder assignment. Georgia has more ways to finish drives Gunner Stockton completed 72.4% of his passes with 22 touchdowns and four interceptions through 11 games before Georgia Tech. He can lean on a running game that averaged 201.6 rushing yards per game over that stretch. This gives Georgia room to keep using play-action and forces Texas to defend the entire playbook on early downs. The best test comes inside the 20. The Georgia offense scored touchdowns on 44 of 57 red-zone trips through 11 games. Texas allowed touchdowns on just 11 of 31 opponent trips in the regular season. The Longhorns can keep this close if defensive coordinator Will Muschamp’s group forces field goals. Texas won six straight to finish the regular season and allowed 15.6 points per game. That defense has earned the benefit of the doubt. But field goals supplied nine of Texas’ 16 points at Kyle Field . If Georgia finishes a couple of drives with touchdowns, the Longhorns may have to put the ball in Manning’s hands more often and give Georgia’s pass rush more chances . The Bulldogs can build drive

item.title: Wales end Nations Championship with hearty Japan win
item.description: Nations Championship Wales (26) 40 Tries: Adams 2, Murray, Morgan-Williams, Morgan 2 Cons: Costelow 5 Japan (0) 10 Tries: Komura, Vailea Wales finished their Nations Championship campaign with another victory against Japan in a six-try display at the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham. Wing Josh Adams and replacement flanker Jac Morgan claimed two tries apiece, with full-back Blair Murray and scrum-half Reuben Morgan-Williams also dotting down, while player of the match Sam Costelow kicked 10 points. This set up the most comprehensive margin of victory of the Steve Tandy coaching era in a match that was affected by the miserable conditions. Despite the scoreline, Wales again spent large periods of the game defending against a weakened Japan side who managed two late tries through replacements Shinya Komura and Halatoa Vailea. Returning flanker James Botham made 38 tackles as he equalled Dafydd Jenkins' world record effort in the 35-28 win against New Zealand, a mark they now both share with Thierry Dusautoir of France. It was a curious contest, low on quality, played in front of a half-empty Twickenham as part of a double-header before England faced New Zealand. The victory means Wales secured ninth in the inaugural Nations Championship and finished the year ninth in World Rugby's rankings. It was a second win in the space of three weeks against Japan, and a third victory in a November campaign that will forever be remembered for Wales beating New Zealand for the first time in 73 years. Wales struggle to create early energy Wales had unconvincingly defeated Japan 28-21 in the opening game of the November series, following up that with the famous win against the All Blacks before a narrow loss to Australia. Both Wales and Japan had finished fifth in their respective hemisphere sections to set up a fifth contest between Wales and Japan inside 17 months. Eddie Jones' side had suffered heavy 60-point defeats to England and Scotland and were down to the bare bones with flanker Tiennan Costley named on the wing. Wales initially made five changes with Morgan-Williams making his first Test start and prop Rhys Carre, hooker Ryan Elias, lock Adam Beard and Botham also included. With hooker Dewi Lake and Morgan dropping to the bench, lock Dafydd Jenkins captained the side for the first time in more than two years. There was another late alteration when wing Louis Rees-Zammit was ruled out because of illness, with Scarlets back Ellis Mee promoted from the bench for his first action of this November campaign. With tickets sold for both games there was a sparse crowd when the two sides came out and there was the unusual sound of being able to hear the players on the field when the match started. After the Principality Stadium cauldrons of the past couple of weeks, Tandy told his side they had to create their own atmosphere and energy. item.title: Hamburger SV vs. Bayern Munich: Match discussion, Game time thread, How to watch
item.description: Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images | Getty Images 52’ — Konrad Laimer replaces Lennart Karl. 50’ — Tom Bischof tries another long shot but misses the target. 48’ — Jonas Urbig heads the ball off the line after the ball came off Josip Stanisic’s foot. 46’ — Second half is underway. Luis Díaz replaces Bara Sapoko Ndiaye. Halftime Observations Bayern playing well below standards today. They’re once again presented with a low block and guess what? They’ve created nothing again. Too many passes around the box and poor decision making all around, what a terrible sight. The team has unironically done well against the counterattacks, but has zero ideas going forward. Lennart Karl has been uninspiring and it’s becoming an annoying habit. It’s a moment of madness with Joshua Kimmich. The Bayern captain fell for the classic bait in the form of an off-the-ball foul and got himself sent off. It’s petulant from Kimmich but you gotta feel for him a little: the player who provoked him got away without getting carded. It’s literally Viking all over again. 45+2’ — Halftime. 45’ — One minute added on. 44’ — RED CARD! Joshua Kimmich is sent off after pulling the hair of a Hamburg player. 24’ — Tom Bischof tries his luck from distance but shoots wide of the far post. 23’ — Kim makes a smart block to stop Patson Daka from breaking away. 20’ — Bara Sapoko Ndiaye snuck in behind the Hamburg defence but fires wide of the target. 9’ — Noah Codjo-Evora fires into the side netting. Bayern still probing for an opening goal. 4’ — A Hamburg counterattack comes to nothing thanks to an intervention from Kim Min-jae. 3’ — Lennart Karl fires a loose ball that deflects over the bar. Kickoff! — LET’S GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO!!!!! Lineups are out! Noah Codjo-Evora makes his starting debut for Bayern today and he is joined by Bara Sapoko Ndiaye and Sacha Boey in the starting XI. Bastian Assomo, Tim Binder and Maycon Cardozo join Luis Díaz, Konrad Laimer and Dayot Upamecano on the bench. Die 𝒆𝒓𝒔𝒕𝒆𝒏 𝑬𝒍𝒇 für #HSVFCB ! 📋 pic.twitter.com/eEdS7e6hTc — FC Bayern München (@FCBayern) November 28, 2026 Bayern Munich is in disarray at the moment. The Bavarians are fresh off a 2-1 defeat in the Champions League amidst a whirlwind of mayhem off the pitch, threatening to derail the season. The onus is on the team to respond with a statement win against Hamburg, but it won’t be as easy. Hamburg is also reeling from a crushing defeat: a 4-0 loss in the Nordderby to Werder Bremen is probably on the same magnitude as Bayern’s Champions League loss as far as the Rothosen are concerned. Both teams have a point to prove, the question is who will? Bayern is rocking a decimated squad at the moment, which means results will be harder to get. Can they defy the odds again, or will the midweek loss spiral into something more damaging? item.title: Bucks add games against Jazz and Raptors to schedule
item.description: Following the conclusion of preliminary NBA Cup play late on Nov. 27, the league added two regular-season games to the December schedule for teams that did not advance to the knockout rounds of the in-season tournament. The Milwaukee Bucks were one of those teams, and they had games against the Utah Jazz and Toronto Raptors added to their schedule. Milwaukee will head to Utah on Dec. 6 for a 4 p.m. CT game and host the Raptors on Dec. 10 at 7 p.m. CT. The Jazz game is an interesting addition, as the Bucks already had a trip to Salt Lake City on their schedule Jan. 26 as part of a West Coast trip. The game against the Raptors also will be the team's fourth meeting of the season and second at Fiserv Forum. The teams already have played twice, including the Bucks' second win of the season on Nov. 23. This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Bucks add games against Jazz and Raptors to schedule

item.title: Skip Bayless says Cowboys would’ve won vs Eagles if they had made the Dak Prescott trade he told them to
item.description: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images Skip Bayless has continued to express his displeasure for Dak Prescott on the back of the Dallas Cowboys losing to the Philadelphia Eagles. The Cowboys are now 5-7 for the season after giving up 21 points against the Eagles, meaning there is a strong chance they will now go three years in a row without reaching the postseason. But rather than questioning Dallas’ defence, which is the worst in the league right now, Bayless has instead spoken of his desire to trade Dak Prescott for Jayden Daniels. Skip Bayless thinks Jayden Daniels would have helped the Dallas Cowboys beat the Philadelphia Eagles Bayless already commented on his desire to trade Prescott for Daniels prior to the November trade deadline. Speaking in late October, he said: “If they want to trade me Jayden Daniels for Dak Prescott. It’s done. Straight up, player for player. Let me have him, I’ll take it. He was available all last year when we went 7-9-1. He’s been available this year; we’re 2-4. Give me Jayden Daniels.” Now, on the latest episode of Gridiron, Bayless has once again been speaking about trading for Daniels and this time claimed that the quarterback ‘gets that game home’ [against the Eagles]. He said: “If there’s some way that Washington would trade me Jayden Daniels straight up for Dak Prescott, which they would laugh at, I would do it in a heartbeat because I’ve got 25 years old versus 33, and I’ve got the clutch gene versus no clutch gene. That’s just me.” His fellow host replied: “Yeah, and you still would have lost 38-39 yesterday,” seeing Skip respond by suggesting Daniels would have won them the game. He said: “No, I would not have. Jayden Daniels gets that game home. He’s going to just keep on keeping on in the fourth quarter. He’s going to throw two more touchdown passes in the fourth quarter.” While Skip seems keen to move on from Prescott, Daniels’ stats have not been that impressive this season. He has 1,788 passing yards (3,340 for Dak), 10 passing touchdowns versus 27 for the Cowboys star and has a completion rate of 64.9% compared to 65.8% for Prescott. Bayless also mentioned Daniels having a ‘clutch gene’, which may be the only area he actually has the better of the Dallas QB. Prescott is 2-5 in postseason games throughout his career, while the Washington Commanders star is 2-1. The 8-3 Cardinals (7-2 in the ACC) have been rewarded for their fine form and enter Thanksgiving weekend following another rise up the rankings, with the faintest of hopes at making this year’s College Football Playoff. The Wildcats won five editions of this annual rivalry prior to 2024, since which Louisville has outscored Kentucky 82-14 across the past two meetings. And all the momentum is currently running in favor of Jeff Brohm’s men, whose opponents are in the midst of a three-loss streak that has seen them lose their spot in the rankings. Kentucky once again failed to flatter at Missouri last weekend, losing 28-14 in the wake of back-to-back defeats against Tennessee (then No. 13) and Florida. It’s been a steep drop-off for first-year head coach Will Stein after his side were ranked sixth at the start of November, averaging just 11.3 points scored across the past three games. Louisville’s average of 38.6 points scored per game this season puts them eighth in the country, inspired by the duel threat of quarterback Lincoln Kienholz, who has 20 passing touchdowns and 11 rushing this term. item.title: GB miss out on Davis Cup final as Alcaraz stars for Spain
item.description: Great Britain were unable to give Leon Smith the perfect send-off as Davis Cup captain as Carlos Alcaraz inspired Spain to a 2-0 victory in the semi-finals. Competing in their first Davis Cup semi-final since 2019, Britain fell short as Arthur Fery was unable to match the dazzling brilliance of Alcaraz, with the seven-time major winner surging to an emphatic 6-2 6-1 win. That was after rising star Rafael Jodar defeated Cameron Norrie 6-2 7-5 in the opening singles match to put Spain in the driving seat in Bologna. The defeat brings the curtain down on Smith's near 17-year tenure as captain, during which he led Britain to Davis Cup success in 2015. Spain captain David Ferrer, who is also stepping down after this year's tournament, will have the chance to guide his nation to their first Davis Cup title since 2019 when they face Italy in Sunday's final. Three-time defending champions Italy beat Spain in last year's final , although they are without talisman and world number two Jannik Sinner because of a wrist injury that will keep him out of the Australian Open. "It is a second straight final, it is going to be my first Davis Cup final, I'll do whatever it takes to win," said Alcaraz. "It's something I have been chasing for a really long time, to be in a Davis Cup final." Alcaraz back to brilliant best against Fery as Norrie loses After Norrie's defeat by Jodar, Fery was faced with the mammoth task of beating world number three Alcaraz - a player he had never faced before. Alcaraz lifted his first ATP Finals title six days earlier, a triumph that completed his astonishing return to the sport following four months out with a wrist injury. And his return to top form was on full display as he dismantled Fery, ranked 32nd, in a dominant first set in which he dropped just two points behind his first serve. Alcaraz's movement and shot-making continued to dazzle the crowd in Italy and Fery could do little to stop the Spaniard's sprint to the finish line. Alcaraz started the season by becoming the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam with his Australian Open triumph, and now has the chance to end the year with his first Davis Cup title, one of the few trophies he has yet to win. For Fery, who enjoyed his career-best season and a fairytale run to the Wimbledon semi-finals, it was another harsh reminder of the gulf in class between himself and the game's top players after he fell in straight sets to world number one Alexander Zverev in Thursday's quarter-final. Great Britain had not reached the final of the Davis Cup since they won the tournament in 2015 [Getty Images] World number 10 Jodar has established himself as one of the brightest talents in men's tennis in 2026, having started the year outside the top 150. In the past 12 months he has made his Grand Slam debut, won a first ATP title and experienced a meteoric rise up the rankings, which saw him qualify for the end-of-season ATP Finals, reserved for the year's top eight performing men. item.title: Can Puka Nacua return to Rams this year?
item.description: The Puka Nacua injury is fascinating in terms of the varying reports to how long it will take him to recover. At this point, sit back and see what happens. It seems no one knows how long Puka will be out, when he’ll be back, how long he’ll be a Ram via extension or not. It’s fascinating. Report: Rams haven’t completely ruled out Puka Nacua returning in playoffs (ramswire) “On Saturday, though, Tom Pelissero of The Ringer shared a new update that the Rams “haven’t completely closed the door on Puka Nacua returning in the playoffs.” That being said, the Rams “aren’t expecting” to get him back for the postseason, which is essentially what McVay said in the first place.“ NFL insider shares unexpected optimistic Puka Nacua update for Rams (sportingnews) “The Rams haven’t completely closed the door on Puka Nacua returning in the playoffs,” Pelissero reports. “But they aren’t expecting to get their star receiver back from surgery for a complete MCL tear that wasn’t a routine injury.” This is an interesting update for the Rams with Nacua. While the team is expecting Nacua to miss the rest of the regular season and all of the playoffs, a late playoff return isn’t totally impossible. His surgery will take months to recover from, but if the Rams could make a run to the Super Bowl, Nacua might have a small chance of suiting up by then if his recovery is going well and he’s ahead of schedule.“ Dianna Russini reveals NFL GMs’ thoughts on Puka Nacua’s long-term future with LA Rams (sports.yahoo) “Puka Nacua has been a revelation since the LA Rams drafted him in 2023, setting rookie records with 105 catches for 1,486 yards. This season, before his season-ending injury, Nacua posted 70 receptions for 715 receiving yards and 4 receiving touchdowns across 7 games played. His on-field production has never been an issue, yet his future remains uncertain. Playing out the final year of his rookie contract, Nacua is a free agent this coming offseason, and there is some speculation about his future within the league’s power circles.“ Rams not giving up hope for Puka Nacua returning from injury in time for playoffs (clutchpoints) “Puka Nacua’s 2026 NFL season has been a tale of production derailed by injury and off-field discipline. Before his injury, the fourth-year wideout remained Matthew Stafford’s most reliable chain-mover and high-volume target. He appeared in seven games and racked up 70 receptions for 715 yards and four touchdowns. However, Nacua’s year was persistently interrupted by lower-body ailments. These culminated in Week 9 when he suffered a complete MCL tear in his right knee. Nacua eventually underwent MCL surgery during the Rams’ Week 11 bye. item.title: “Bro Is Begging for a Trophy”: NBA Fans Erupt as Victor Wembanyama Makes MVP Statement After Beating Luka Doncic and Lakers
item.description: Victor Wembanyama © @spurs/X The San Antonio Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama and the Los Angeles Lakers’ Luka Doncic faced off in a highly anticipated NBA Cup matchup on Friday night, with Wembanyama and the Spurs pulling out a 99-96 victory. The showdown pitted two of the Western Conference’s top teams and MVP frontrunners against one another, and it wasn’t decided until late in the fourth quarter. Early on, the Lakers held a firm grip on the contest, leading by as many as 20 points, before a second-half surge allowed San Antonio to hang on for a crucial win and advance to the NBA Cup knockout round. Not only did the Spurs prove they can beat one of the best teams in the league, but throughout the season, they have shown they can win in multiple ways. Following the game, the Spurs center opened up about how San Antonio plans to keep piling up wins this season before making a statement about his individual goals. “Dominate the rim. On offense, my teammates are open. You know, this is how we’ve won many games last year, and this is how we’re going to win many games this year. I’m going to have to take the mid-range shot, especially in late-game isolations and stuff, and the threes, of course. But dominating the rim on both sides is how I’m going to win MVP one day,” Wembanyama said on Nightcap. However, his comments did not sit well with everyone. While Wembanyama has been one of the league’s most dominant two-way forces through the first 20 games, several fans, particularly rival supporters, took issue with his remarks. Some felt it was too early in the season for him to talk about winning MVP, particularly after a night when his performance left a lot to be desired. “Bro is begging for a trophy lol,” one fan wrote. This is not the first time Wembanyama has publicly spoken about his MVP ambitions; last season, he also voiced his case before finishing third in the voting. While it is still early in the 2026-27 campaign and plenty can change, Wembanyama and the Spurs have already stacked several measuring-stick victories. Doncic had held the top spot on the league’s MVP ladder over the last four updates with Wembanyama right behind at No. 2, a hierarchy that could shift following Friday’s head-to-head result. Victor Wembanyama Makes Hilarious Shaq Admission After Free-Throw Struggle Despite racking up a double-double of 25 points and 16 rebounds along with four steals and two blocks, Wembanyama endured too many misfires from 15 feet, converting just 3-of-8 attempts. After the game, Wembanyama addressed the free-throw lapses and poked fun at himself by invoking Hall of Fame center Shaquille O’Neal, famously one of the NBA’s worst free-throw shooters. “I guess I’m just like Shaq free-throw line shooting wise,” Wembanyama joked. It is a fair assessment, as Wembanyama is shooting a career-worst 77.8% from the free-throw line, a 4.9% drop from last season’s 82.7%. item.title: 2027: Nigerians determined to vote out APC, says Hashim
item.description: Presidential candidate of the Accord Party, Dr. Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has declared that Nigerians have made up their minds to vote against the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general election, accusing the President Bola Tinubu-led administration of worsening the country’s economic and security challenges. Hashim made the declaration on Saturday in Abuja during the flag-off of his presidential campaign, where he promised to build a $4 trillion economy within eight years if elected president. He said economic hardship, rising insecurity, widespread poverty and what he described as the significant collapse of the economy under the APC-led government had strengthened Nigerians’ determination to change the country’s leadership. The Accord presidential candidate cited the reported reach of his recent interview on Symfoni Podcast, which he said was watched by almost 10 million Nigerians and attracted over one million positive reactions, as evidence of growing interest in his presidential ambition. He also alleged that some APC leaders were complicit in the worsening security situation, saying banditry and other forms of criminality had devastated communities across several states. According to him, the 2027 general election would be different, insisting that political victory would not be determined by the ability of parties to fill stadiums during campaigns. He accused the ruling party of already campaigning against itself through its handling of the country’s affairs. “Nigerians will cook APC with cold water,” Hashim declared in Hausa, drawing a loud ovation from the crowd. He further accused the APC of attempting to manipulate the 2027 elections and criticised what he described as exorbitant charges for political campaign billboards in Abuja. However, Hashim ruled out violence as a means of pursuing his presidential ambition, assuring supporters that his campaign would remain peaceful. “We will not resort to violence from our side. We will not incite anybody. I don’t want to lose any of my supporters,” he said. On the economy, the presidential candidate promised that an Accord-led government would restore Nigeria’s economic prosperity, reduce the cost of petroleum products and electricity, and introduce policies that would make energy more affordable. He cited Kuwait and other oil-producing countries as examples of nations where citizens enjoy more affordable energy despite the availability of petroleum resources. Hashim recalled that Nigeria built refineries during the administration of the late Prime Minister, Tafawa Balewa, arguing that the country could achieve significantly better economic results through responsible leadership and prudent management of public resources. He said the party would officially unveil its manifesto the following week, promising comprehensive policy proposals covering telecommunications, information and communications technology, industrialisation, youth empowerment, employment generation, defence

item.title: Texas Tech football 2027 opener vs USC officially set in Las Vegas
item.description: The long-awaited announcement of the Texas Tech football 2027 season opener has finally dropped. The Red Raiders will square off with the Southern California Trojans on Friday, Aug. 27, at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Nevada. The matchup was revealed Saturday, Nov. 28, on the FOX Big Noon Kickoff pre-game show. The game will be televised on FOX. Tech and Southern Cal have played three times. USC beat the Red Raiders in 1978 in Los Angeles, in 1979 in Lubbock and at the end of the 1994 season in the Cotton Bowl. The College Football Playoff's expansion to 24 teams next season will require Power Four teams to play 10 games against one another to be eligible for a berth. Texas Tech would meet that requirement for 2027 by playing USC along with the usual nine-game Big 12 schedule. The Red Raiders have nonconference home games next September against Arkansas-Pine Bluff and New Mexico. Tech still needs a Power Four opponent each season for 2028 and 2029, holes in the schedule that came about when Mississippi State canceled a home-and-home series against the Red Raiders. This article originally appeared on Lubbock Avalanche-Journal: Texas Tech football 2027 opener vs USC officially set in Las Vegas

item.title: Urban Meyer Takes Brutal Shot at Michigan Football Ahead of Ohio State Showdown
item.description: Former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer certainly isn’t holding back when it comes to his assessment of Michigan football heading into Saturday’s rivalry showdown. Meyer delivered a brutal assessment of the Wolverines’ offense, while surprisingly admitting that Michigan’s defense concerns him more than anything else heading into The Game. Meyer also weighed in on the future of Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood, suggesting that the former five-star recruit could generate significant interest from other programs should he decide to leave Ann Arbor. Legendary Florida football coach Urban Meyer watches the action during first half of an NCAA football game at Steve Spurrier Field at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium in Gainesville, FL on Saturday, November 7, 2026. [Alan Youngblood/Gainesville Sun] Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Urban Meyer Calls Michigan’s Offense ‘Pathetic’ As reported by Phil Harrison of Buckeyes Wire , Meyer didn’t mince words when discussing Michigan’s offensive struggles. However, his criticism came while explaining why he was so impressed with the Wolverines’ defense. “That offense is pathetic up there,” Meyer said. “It’s the worst offense in college football.” Interestingly, despite believing Ohio State has the more talented roster, Meyer believes Michigan’s defense is the best-performing unit on either team. He specifically pointed to the Wolverines’ performance in their 18-16 triple-overtime victory over previously undefeated UCLA. “The roster’s better — Ohio State — but the best unit performing right now is the Wolverine defense. And that concerns me a little bit. They really hammered UCLA. You got to think, the other side of the ball for the Wolverines is terrible — they’re last in the country. And so, to still have decent numbers — only one team has over 21 points on them all year, and that was Oregon — that’s a legit defense.” Urban Meyer Weighs In on Bryce Underwood’s Future Despite his criticism of Michigan’s offense, Meyer had some encouraging things to say about Underwood, who has been dealing with a lower-body injury heading into Saturday’s game. Speaking on The Triple Option podcast , Meyer praised the quarterback’s ability to navigate the adversity he has faced since committing to Michigan. “I’m not sure, in recent history at a blue blood school, has a quarterback ever gone through so much controversy,” Meyer said. “He’s committed to a place that completely falls apart… And yet somehow he finds a way and has enough character and toughness to throw the game winning ball (against UCLA)… His value, I think, around the country if he decides to leave, if he plays his heart out this week, his value is very, very high.” Underwood, who was expected to start against Ohio State , has an opportunity to silence some of his critics with a strong performance in Columbus. item.title: Monaco striker Paris Brunner ruled out to face Lyon and possibly for several weeks
item.description: Monaco striker Paris Brunner ruled out to face Lyon and possibly for several weeks AS Monaco’s Paris Brunner (20) is set to miss this Sunday’s away match against Olympique Lyonnais, on Matchday 12 of Ligue 1, as announced by his manager Filipe Luis at a press conference. Having already missed ASM’s Conference League victory over Heart of Midlothian (2-3) on Thursday evening, the striker is suffering from a hamstring injury. This is a particularly tough blow for the Monegasques, as the German U21 international’s situation remains highly uncertain. “There is still some uncertainty regarding his condition. The doctors are currently discussing the matter and we are awaiting further information,” explained Luis. “He’d only just returned from international duty, having put in a considerable effort. He played in the rain, and there’s also a new training regime; that could explain what happened to him. He played the full 90 minutes the other day (against Auxerre, 1-1, last Saturday), then felt this pain. We must continue to work on preventing injuries.” When asked about the possibility that Brunner might not return to Ligue 1 action before 2027, his manager chose to be cautious, stating that he preferred to “wait a little while to get more precise information.” Having made a sensational start to the season with ASM, the Dortmund-born player has scored eight goals and provided one assist in 14 matches across all competitions. GFFN | Léo Aschi

item.title: Highlands girls basketball's Erilynn Walker voted Express-News Athlete of the Week
item.description: Highlands' Erilynn Walker Shots a jump shot during the first quarter against Burbank in a District 27-5A girls basketball game on Tuesday, Jan. 20, 2026. (Charlie Blalock/Contributor) Highlands sophomore Erilynn Walker was a walking double-double at the Southside girls basketball tournament. Now, she's waltzed into Express-News Athlete of the Week honors. Walker averaged 16.4 points and 15.2 rebounds for the Owls, who went 4-1 and finished third in the tournament. She recorded double-doubles in each of the five games and was selected to the all-tournament team. She had a standout game against Boerne Champion, scoring 19 points and securing 21 rebounds. Her stellar performance last week earned her Girls Basketball Player of the Week honors on Monday, and she beat out three fellow finalists in the Athlete of the Week poll. Marshall senior Jason Vidaurri, the Boys Basketball Player of the Week, averaged 13 points, 9.6 assists, 6.1 rebounds and 5.3 steals last week. He scored 20 points with 17 assists, six rebounds and seven steals in a 71-59 win over Austin LASA. Medina Valley junior slot back Kevin Straughter, the Offensive Player of the Week, rushed for four touchdowns and 241 yards on only five carries, averaging an eye-popping 48.2 yards per tote in a 56-14 playoff win over Corpus Christi Carroll. Brennan junior linebacker Johnas Brewster recorded a season-high 26 tackles, including 20 solo stops, in a 31-15 playoff win over Weslaco. Brewster had four TFLs and two sacks to help the Bears advance. The Defensive Player of the Week then helped the Bears slow down Austin Lake Travis on Friday in a 24-17 victory that secured a spot in the state quarterfinals. item.title: U23s kick off second half of the season with last-minute win
item.description: U23s kick off second half of the season with last-minute win Team news Arne Wessels returned to the starting line-up for the derby against VfL Bochum after serving a suspension for accumulated yellow cards. Fadi Zarqelain initially dropped to the bench to make way for the attacking player. BVB coach Daniel Rios also made two further changes to the side that beat Sportfreunde Lotte 2-0: Luca Reggiani and Enzo dos Santos came in for Nanitonda Quiala and Tim Degener. Match report The 1,346 spectators at Stadion Rote Erde witnessed an intense contest from the outset, with both teams looking to make their mark. The visitors from Bochum registered the first shot through Luis Pick in the fifth minute. But BVB also threatened early on: a driven cross from left-back Finn Fuchs was cleared just in front of the goal line before the lurking Diego Ngambia could reach the ball (8). The U23s increasingly took control of the game, repeatedly causing Bochum problems down the left through the lively Arne Wessels. That was also how the opening goal came about: Connor Krempicki met a Wessels cross with a first-time finish to put BVB ahead (18), his shot taking a decisive deflection. BVB celebrated again in the 26th minute, but Kevin Mutove's goal following fine work by Ngambia was ruled out because the striker was offside. BVB kept up the pressure and created further chances. First, Ngambia narrowly failed to connect with another excellent Wessels cross (30), before Malik Hodroj curled the ball over the visitors' goal (36). Just before the break, VfL, who repeatedly found opportunities on the counter, gained more of a foothold and had further efforts, none of which troubled Silas Ostrzinski. After the break, Bochum struck, ruthlessly punishing an error by Ostrzinski. Under no pressure, Dortmund's goalkeeper played the ball straight to Lasse Isbruch, who slotted home to make it 1-1 (56). Following the equaliser, BVB tried to regain their rhythm by keeping more possession. Rios also introduced two fresh players in Tim Degener and Fadi Zarqelain. Despite their territorial advantage, Dortmund initially struggled to get into dangerous shooting positions against a well-organised Bochum side. Efforts from Enzo dos Santos (68), Fuchs (76) and Degener (82) lacked the necessary threat. BVB had a let-off late on when a shot from Lirim Jashari struck the post (84). Shortly afterwards, substitute Kegni squandered BVB's best chance at the other end. The forward was denied from close range by a sharp save from the visiting goalkeeper (87). With the final action of the game, Ayman Azhil secured victory for the Black & Yellows after all. Dortmund's captain converted a penalty to make it 2-1 and spark jubilant celebrations, after Bochum's Till Winkelmann had brought down Luca Reggiani. After the final whistle, Bochum coach Heiko Butscher was shown a red card for protesting loudly to the referee about the penalty decision. With this narrow victory, the U23s delivered what their coach

item.title: 'Still gutted': UTSA fans react to reports Jeff Traylor is headed to Baylor
item.description: Head coach Jeff Traylor of the UTSA Roadrunners celebrates after the game against the North Texas Mean Green at the Alamodome on November 14, 2026 in San Antonio, Texas. (Zach Del Bello/Getty Images) UTSA fans had plenty to celebrate after Friday's win. But reports linking coach Jeff Traylor to Baylor left many wondering if he'll be with the Roadrunners for their championship game next week. CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reported Baylor is set to hire Traylor as its next head coach. ESPN's Pete Thamel reported the two sides are working toward a deal that could be finalized in the coming days. On Reddit, one UTSA fan wrote , "Felt inevitable, but still gutted," adding that after seven seasons, it was hard to picture the program without Traylor. Another hoped he would stay for one more game: "Hope he sticks around for next weeks champ game." A commenter in r/CFB who identified as a San Antonio native said they wished the city had rallied behind UTSA more. On Baylor's subreddit , a commenter pointed to Traylor's Texas roots and his ability to win with fewer resources as reasons to be excited about the reported hire. The reaction on X was mixed, too. "63-28 at UTSA and Baylor finally came knocking. Those fans knew this day was coming," @beckersportsnet wrote. Nico, @garcia54832 via X, said Traylor "should have stayed in SA," calling San Antonio "the greatest city in America." Some posts questioned the timing of the reported move. "Baylor should be punished for contacting a coach before the season is complete," @sstaedtler8787 wrote. @cbelnap added, "Baylor should face sanctions for tampering with a coach in the middle of a season." Others challenged Traylor's past comments about staying. "I thought he said he wasn't leaving and that San Antonio was the greatest city in the country," @MeyekOnRoute66 wrote. @moraltreason posted, "Traylor said he wasn't leaving. Let's see if he is a man of his word." And @mrrockjunior warned UTSA fans not to "talk in absolutes regarding college football." UTSA beat Tulsa, 28-22, Friday to finish the season 10-2 and earn the right to host the American Conference title game Dec. 5 at the Alamodome. Traylor has not said whether he will coach that game. After Friday's win, he said his attention was on the championship matchup. Traylor has led UTSA for seven seasons, guiding the Roadrunners to Conference USA titles in 2021 and 2022 . Now, fans are waiting to see whether he will lead them one more time. Sign up for Afternoon Headlines, MySA's free newsletter bringing you San Antonio's top stories of the day. item.title: Michigan vs Ohio State availability report: Bryce Underwood to start
item.description: COLUMBUS, OH − Michigan football will have Bryce Underwood available for "The Game." Underwood, a sophomore who was listed as questionable all week after reportedly suffering a lower body injury in last week's 18-16 3OT win over UCLA, was removed from the Michigan's availability report Saturday morning provided to the Big Ten. He will start against Ohio State at Ohio Stadium. The Ohio State-Michigan football start time is noon and the TV channel is Fox. FOLLOW ALONG: Michigan vs Ohio State live updates, highlights U-M had as many as players listed as questionable earlier this week, but only two in reserves, sophomore Nathaniel Owusu Boateng and freshman Jaylen Pile have been ruled out. The rest, including Underwood, who coach Kyle Whittingham said would be the starter earlier in the week appear set to suit up in Columbus. "Bryce is the guy,” Whittingham said Monday. “Bryce is the guy and Tommy [Carr] is No. 2 barring anything unforeseen." Underwood has struggled much of this season, including the past three starts where he's completed fewer than 50% of his passes in each contest. As much was the case last week when Underwood made his first start in more than a month and completed 11 of 24 passes for 127 yards and one touchdown while also connecting with Jalen Hoffman for the game-winning two-point conversion. Underwood is also looking to re-write his script against Ohio State after he was shutdown by the Buckeyes a year ago in a 27-9 loss in Ann Arbor. He completed 8 of 18 passes for 63 yards and an interception on that day. MICHIGAN VS OSU PICKS: Who can salvage season with win in The Game? Michigan injury report vs Ohio State OUT: LB Nathaniel Owusu Boateng WR Jaylen Pile WR JJ Buchanan WR Braydon Alford RB Micah Ka'apana DE Julius Holly OL Ace Hamilton OL Andrew Sprague DE Nate Marshall Michigan football QB Bryce Underwood has been removed from the availability report and appears good to go against Ohio State. pic.twitter.com/3LpHzgefN3 — Tony Garcia | Detroit Free Press (@RealTonyGarcia) November 28, 2026 U-M is more healthy than it has been, as running back Jordan Marshall, safety Rod Moore edge John Henry Daley, offensive linemen Blake Frazier and Brady Norton and tight end Hoffman were all removed from the availability report. Marshall, a junior from Cincinnati, missed last week against UCLA. He lasted just two series against OSU last year before a shoulder injury prevented him from continuing. Moore, a sixth-year senior and three-time captain, has missed the past two games against the Buckeyes − he's 3-0 in the rivalry in games he has played in. Perhaps most notably for a banged up O-line, it could be back at full strength with Frazier and Norton both set to return after missing the UCLA game (Frazier was also out against Oregon). Tony Garcia is the Michigan beat writer for the Detroit Free Press. Email him at apgarcia@freepress.com and follow him on X at @RealTonyGarcia . item.title: F1 Qatar GP: Kimi Antonelli completes practice clean sweep as Mercedes dominates
item.description: Motorsport photo Kimi Antonelli has handed Mercedes a clean sweep of Qatar GP practice sessions as the Silver Arrows head to qualifying with a huge advantage. Russell went quickest before halfway as teams embarked on soft-tyre runs with Mercedes continuing its ominous form on the high-downforce motorcycle circuit of Lusail, only for Antonelli to take another chunk out of that laptime in the second half. Unlike Friday's twice red-flagged FP2 session, third practice took place without incident, which was partly thanks to a tepid start with little to no action early on. At the start, Pierre Gasly circulated by himself, making up for lost ground after beaching his Alpine in the gravel midway through Friday's second practice. Gasly was eventually joined by team-mate Franco Colapinto and Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas, while the others stayed in the garage for the first third of the session. That all changed suddenly before the 20-minute mark as the heavy hitters embarked on soft-tyre runs - a compound projected to be only useful for qualifying. The race is expected to be completed on medium and hard Pirelli tyres, which are facing their most demanding weekend on the Lusail loop. As qualifying simulations got underway, outgoing world champion Lando Norris headed to the Turn 14 escape road after catching a violent snap of oversteer. As was the case during both of Friday's practice endeavours, Mercedes immediately took charge with George Russell's 1m22.983s leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli. That was over half a second better than what McLaren's Oscar Piastri and Max Verstappen could muster, the latter driving a Red Bull RB22 which required rebalancing after a tougher free practice outing. While Russell then drifted wide in Turn 5, Antonelli's second mid-session run yielded a time almost identical to his team-mate's, just 0.017s off. George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes With 15 minutes to go, Verstappen briefly claimed top before Antonelli immediately retaliated and restored Mercedes' comfortable half-second cushion with a 1m22.400s effort. Russell had no answer for that flash of pace, conceding 0.249s. Verstappen remained third, a sobering 0.501s in arrears as the first non-Mercedes car, followed by team-mate Isack Hadjar. After a Friday which Charles Leclerc described as "very difficult", there was little progress for Ferrari as Leclerc took fifth, eight tenths behind Antonelli. McLaren also struggled more than was expected with sixth for Norris and seventh for Piastri. Lewis Hamilton fared worse after being held up by traffic on his final hotlap, splitting Racing Bull's midfield leaders Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson in ninth. item.title: Flyers Game 29: Lines, Notes, & How to Watch vs. Islanders
item.description: The Philadelphia Flyers (10-12-6) are back in action on Saturday when they host the New York Islanders (12-8-5) at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Puck Drop is at 7:30 PM ET. The Flyers are coming into the game after a 5-2 win over the Vancouver Canucks, which improved their record over the last 5 games to 4-1-0. While it may not feel that way with the events over the past 2 games, the Flyers have quietly strung together a good stretch. The Islanders come into Saturday following a loss to the Winnipeg Jets on Long Island. They’re 2-2-1 over the last 5 games, and 6-2-2 over their last 10. Puck drop is at 7:30 PM ET at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Here is everything you need to know before the game. Read More: Flyers’ Power Play Shines in 5-2 Black Friday Win vs. Canucks Game Flyers projected Lines & Pairs vs. Islanders Forwards Tyson Foerster – Christian Dvorak – Travis Konecny Owen Tippett – Denver Barkey – Porter Martone Trevor Zegras – Noah Cates – Matvei Michkov Cole Knuble – Sean Couturier – Noel Acciari Defensemen Travis Sanheim – Rasmus Ristolainen Cam York – Jamie Drysdale Nick Seeler – Oliver Bonk Goalie Joseph Woll Dan Vladar Special Teams PP1: Drysdale, Zegras, Barkey, Martone, Michkov PP2: Bonk, Dvorak, Foerster, Tippett, Konecny PK1: Couturier, Dvorak, York, Sanheim PK2: Cates, Foerster, Ristolainen, Seeler Notes There certainly is some outside noise around the team, causing a bit of a distraction. Matvei Michkov was scratched on Friday vs. the Islanders due to an “internal team matter.” Later reports indicated that it was due to an altercation with a teammate, and t hat teammate was reportedly Porter Martone. Both players are expected to be in action on Saturday. Oliver Bonk was also a healthy scratch on Friday, but that one is not alarming. It wasn’t the first time that head coach Rick Tocchet has done this in a back-to-back, citing the fact that Bonk is still young and wanting to give him a bit of a breather/protection while he adjusts to the NHL game. Expect Bonk to have fresh legs and to make a big impact on Saturday. Joseph Woll is expected to get the start on Saturday against the Islander. He was great for about 57 minutes on Wednesday against the Capitals before the wheels fell off at the end of the game, which was not fully his fault. He had won his last 4 starts before that. Look for a big bounce-back from Woll. The Islanders have gotten really good goaltending from Ilya Sorokin and Semyon Varlamov this season. Philly is 27th in goals for per game, while the Islanders are 5th in goals against. It could be a recipe for disaster for the Flyers, even if they have scored at a higher clip lately. item.title: Diamondbacks Add Pitching Depth and Catching Help in Latest Moves
item.description: Arizona Diamondbacks infielder Demetrio Crisantes (5) tracks a pop-up against the Seattle Mariners at Salt River Fields on March 9, 2026. The Arizona Diamondbacks made two notable additions on Friday, agreeing to a one-year, $3 million deal with Japanese right-hander Kona Takahashi and acquiring catcher Henry Davis from the Pittsburgh Pirates in exchange for utilityman Tim Tawa. Takahashi, 29, spent nine seasons with the Seibu Lions of Nippon Professional Baseball. He posted a 2.54 ERA over 138.1 innings in 2026 and brings a ground-ball-heavy approach after more than 1,300 career innings in Japan. As an international free agent with nine years of NPB service, he was not subject to a posting fee. The deal gives Arizona a low-cost rotation option as the club looks to manage payroll while addressing starting pitching depth. Earlier Friday, the Diamondbacks completed a one-for-one trade that sent Tawa to Pittsburgh for Davis, the former No. 1 overall pick in the 2021 draft. Davis has yet to establish himself as a regular in the majors but provides additional catching depth behind the current group. Tawa, a versatile utility player, hit .240 with a .662 OPS in 351 plate appearances last season. These moves follow Arizona’s Nov. 20 acquisition of right-hander Johan Oviedo from the Boston Red Sox in exchange for left-handed pitching prospect Luke Dotson and a player to be named later or cash. The club has also selected the contracts of several prospects, including outfielder Druw Jones, and non-tendered left-handers Andrew Saalfrank and Blake Walston. With Corbin Burnes, Eduardo Rodríguez, Merrill Kelly, Brandon Pfaadt and Ryne Nelson still projected in the rotation, Takahashi and Oviedo add depth at a modest combined cost. The Diamondbacks enter the winter with multiple free agents from the 2026 roster, including Zac Gallen and Kevin Ginkel, while fielding trade interest in some of their established starters. General manager Mike Hazen’s group has prioritized affordable pitching additions so far while remaining open to further roster tweaks.

item.title: SC Freiburg vs. RB Leipzig preview: Top-four rivals meet in the Black Forest
item.description: SC Freiburg vs. RB Leipzig preview: Top-four rivals meet in the Black Forest Freiburg Freiburg have enjoyed an outstanding start to the campaign and head into Sunday's contest sitting third in the Bundesliga table, having collected 22 points from their opening 10 matches. Julian Schuster's side have continued to build on last season's progress and are currently enjoying a six-match winning streak across all competitions. Their most recent league outing saw them claim a 1-0 victory away to Elversberg, extending their domestic winning run to three matches while keeping another clean sheet. The Black Forest club have also been impressive on home soil, and will be confident of making life difficult for a Leipzig side that has been scoring goals for fun in recent weeks. With just a point separating the two teams, a win would be a more than valuable one for Freiburg as they look to maintain their position in the Champions League places. Team news Schuster is in a relatively comfortable position regarding injuries, with Florent Muslija the only major absentee heading into the weekend. Cyriaque Irie is pushing for a first Bundesliga start of the campaign after scoring twice in his last three appearances. At the same time, Igor Matanovic and Yuito Suzuki will both be expected to play important roles in the attacking third. RB Leipzig RB Leipzig travel to Freiburg in equally impressive form, having established themselves as genuine contenders for the Bundesliga's top positions. Martín Demichelis's men have won their last four league matches and started the weekend in fourth place ,just one point behind Sunday's opponents. Last time out in the Bundesliga, Leipzig produced an emphatic 5-1 victory away to Union Berlin with theirir attacking quality once again proving too much for the opposition. They followed that up with another impressive performance in midweek, beating Lens 3-1 in the Champions League, with Antonio Nusa scoring twice to help secure all three points. Leipzig are currently the Bundesliga's highest-scoring side and will be confident of finding the net against Freiburg. However, they will need to be wary of a home side that has been particularly difficult to break down in recent weeks. A fifth consecutive league victory would see them move above Freiburg and strengthen their position in the race for Champions League football, while keeping them in place for a potential title race - though Demichelis will still be saying that one quietly. Team news Leipzig have a few injury concerns heading into Sunday's encounter, with Marc Guiu, Castello Lukeba and Assan Ouedraogo remaining unavailable, with Lukeba in a race to get fit before the winter break next month. item.title: NFL insider reveals potential timeline for Commanders to play Brandon Aiyuk
item.description: NFL insider reveals potential timeline for Commanders to play Brandon Aiyuk originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Washington Commanders were the only team all offseason, and ever since Brandon Aiyuk filed for reinstatement, that was expected to land the disgruntled veteran wide receiver. After the San Francisco 49ers officially released him on November 23, the Commanders naturally wound up being the team to sign him. But Aiyuk joined the practice squad, not the 53-man roster. Aiyuk likely won't play for Washington right away. But when will he play, if at all, this season? NFL insider Tom Pelissero of The Ringer revealed that Aiyuk, while set to sit for a little while, is expected to play at some point this year. Brandon Aiyuk expected to play for Commanders, but specific week unknown "The Commanders aren't putting a timeline on WR Brandon Aiyuk. But they do expect him to play at some point this season -- his first game action since a major knee injury over two years ago," Pelissero reports. Aiyuk didn't play in the NFL during the 2025 season, as he had problems with the 49ers over his rehab, leading to the 49ers and Aiyuk deciding to go their separate ways. It took a while for the 49ers to actually release Aiyuk, as the veteran receiver didn't file for reinstatement. When he finally did, Aiyuk paved the way to join the Commanders. He's now on their practice squad and could be elevated three times before needing to be added to the 53-man roster. But there's plenty of uncertainty about when that decision might be made. MORE : Solving the Brian Flores puzzle: How Kyle Shanahan finally bested defensive guru in 49ers win Aiyuk hasn't played in the NFL since the 2024 NFL season. There's likely a good amount the Commanders need to see from him before they can confidently put him out on the field. Besides, Aiyuk needs to learn the playbook, get familiar with taking hits after being away for so long, and also build up his chemistry with Jayden Daniels years after they spent time in college together. The 28-year-old wide receiver's timeline to suit up for the Commanders is still unknown. Pelissero did report that the Commanders do expect to play Aiyuk at some point over the final seven weeks of the NFL season. Commanders fans will likely have to wait a little while before seeing Aiyuk actually suit up on game day. That was always expected, as Aiyuk is just getting back to the NFL after more than a year since he last played. item.title: Tennessee Football vs. Vanderbilt: Kickoff Time, TV Channel and Final Game Preview
item.description: Tennessee quarterback George MacIntyre (12) throws the ball during a Tennessee football game against Furman at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., on Sept. 5, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) NASHVILLE, Tenn. — No. 5 Tennessee (9-2, 6-2 SEC) visits Vanderbilt (4-7, 1-7) on Saturday night in the regular-season finale for both programs. The Volunteers enter the matchup seeking their 10th victory and a stronger College Football Playoff résumé. Meanwhile, the Commodores hope to repeat last season’s rivalry upset and finish their campaign on a positive note. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET at FirstBank Stadium. ESPN will televise the game. How to Watch Tennessee vs. Vanderbilt Game information Details Date Saturday, Nov. 28, 2026 Kickoff 7 p.m. ET TV channel ESPN Streaming ESPN App Stadium FirstBank Stadium Location Nashville, Tennessee Matt Schumacker will call the game alongside analyst Aaron Murray. Taylor Davis will provide reports from the sidelines. Additionally, fans can follow Tennessee’s radio broadcast through the Vol Network. Knoxville’s 107.7 FM serves as the flagship station. Tennessee Looks to Continue Late-Season Momentum Tennessee enters Saturday riding a three-game winning streak. Most recently, the Volunteers defeated LSU 27-13 behind another strong defensive performance. The Volunteers recorded eight sacks and 13 tackles for loss against the Tigers. Furthermore, Tennessee limited LSU to 265 total yards while controlling the game defensively. Tennessee has allowed just 26 combined points during its three November victories. That improvement has helped the Volunteers remain firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation. Meanwhile, freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon continues to provide a spark offensively. Brandon rushed for 112 yards and two touchdowns against LSU, including two fourth-quarter scoring runs. The Volunteers will look to maintain that balance against a Vanderbilt defense seeking a stronger finish. Vanderbilt Seeks Another Rivalry Victory Vanderbilt enters the regular-season finale following a 34-27 loss to Florida. However, the Commodores have recent success against Tennessee to build upon. Last season, Vanderbilt defeated Tennessee 45-24 in Knoxville. The victory snapped the Volunteers’ six-game winning streak in the series and gave the Commodores a memorable rivalry triumph. Now, Vanderbilt coach Clark Lea hopes his team can deliver another strong performance against its in-state rival. Additionally, Saturday marks Senior Day for the Commodores. Vanderbilt has announced a sellout at FirstBank Stadium, setting the stage for a lively atmosphere in Nashville. Although Vanderbilt cannot reach bowl eligibility, the Commodores can still finish their season with a meaningful victory. Key Players to Watch Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop enters Saturday with 1,215 rushing yards, the most in the SEC. Bishop has provided the Volunteers with consistent production throughout the season.

item.title: Ole Miss finishes season with fourth straight Egg Bowl win
item.description: OXFORD, MISSISSIPPI - NOVEMBER 27: Trinidad Chambliss #6 of the Mississippi Rebels celebrates after the game after defeating the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on November 27, 2026 in Oxford, Mississippi. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ole Miss overcame a slow offensive start, and once everything clicked, it caused a blowout in the Egg Bowl for a fourth straight win over Mississippi State, 41-17. The Rebels (8-4, 5-4 SEC) could not string together things offensively in the first half scoring only two field goals and trying a desperation 60-yard field goal at the end of the second quarter. Going into the locker room down 10-6, the boo’s were very audible through Vaught-Hemingway, and either those signs of unhappiness from the fans or a fire and brimstone speech from coaches or both lit a collective fire under Ole Miss. In the second half, Ole Miss outscored MSU 35-7 to completely overwhelm the Bulldogs. One of the major turning points in the game was the Blake Purchase interception to give the Rebels an extra possession but also prime field position after the turnover. I still think he scored on the play, but it didn’t really matter when it came to the final score. Trinidad Chambliss had 249 total offensive yards and three touchdowns, and he dealt with drops from his receiving corps early on that stalled drives plus the absence of three running backs from the usual rotation. Give it up to Joshua Dye for stepping up in the season finale going 20 carries for 91 yards and two touchdowns in a workman-like effort. The Ole Miss defense showed its moxie as well with seven sacks and 13 tackles for loss in the game. Suntarine Perkins led the way with 1.5 sacks and three TFL with his potential comeback to Oxford hanging in the air. MSU owned time of possession with 33:22 of the clock and was clearly trying to keep the Ole Miss offense off the field by running the ball for 131 total yards. The Bulldogs couldn’t convert on third downs, however, and the Purchase interception was the rope slipping out of your hands in a tug of war. For a lot of players, Friday was the last time they’ll play in VHS including Chambliss. Many of them will get to say they never lost an Egg Bowl. While the Golden Egg has taken more of a backseat in terms of accomplishment for Ole Miss teams, it is still an important game for fans and for former players. Damn good job the last four years, cheers! Ole Miss will await its bowl game destination next weekend. Current projections have the Rebels in the Reliaquest Bowl in Tampa, Fla. most likely and facing a Big Ten opponent yet to be determined by this Saturday’s games.

item.title: Tinubu’s reforms push Nigeria’s foreign reserves to $54.13bn – City Boy Movement
item.description: The City Boy Movement has hailed the rise in Nigeria’s gross foreign reserves to $54.13 billion, describing the development as evidence of progress under President Bola Tinubu’s economic reform agenda. The group said the reserves had reached their second-highest level on record since 1999, surpassed only by the $62.08 billion peak recorded in September 2008, when the global financial crisis was unfolding. In a statement titled, “Why Tinubu 4+4? Foreign Reserves Edition,” the movement said Nigeria’s foreign reserves had increased significantly under the Tinubu administration, rising from $32.29 billion in May 2023 to $54.13 billion in November 2026. It put the increase at $21.84 billion, representing nearly 68 per cent growth since the President assumed office. According to the group, the latest figures place Nigeria’s foreign reserves above the peak levels recorded in several years, including 2009, 2007, 2013, 2018, 2025, 2019, 2012 and 2014. The movement noted that Nigeria’s reserves peaked at $53.25 billion in 2009, $51.33 billion in 2007, $48.86 billion in 2013 and $47.87 billion in 2018. It added that the $54.13 billion recorded in 2026 represented the highest level since the 2008 global financial crisis. While acknowledging the difficulties associated with the economic reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration, the group argued that the latest reserve figures indicated that the policies were beginning to yield positive results. It said the growth in foreign reserves was an important development in assessing the direction of the economy, expressing optimism that the country was moving towards greater economic prosperity. “The significance is in the history. Even though the reforms have been difficult, the numbers are beginning to tell their own story. We are on the way to prosperity,” the statement said. The movement also expressed appreciation to Tinubu for what it described as progress in the management of the country’s external reserves, reaffirming its support for the President. The figures cited by the group were attributed to data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN). However, the movement’s assessment comes amid continuing public debate over the impact of the Federal Government’s economic reforms, particularly their effects on inflation, living costs, businesses and household welfare. While higher foreign reserves can strengthen a country’s capacity to meet external obligations and support confidence in its economy, the extent to which the increase translates into improved living conditions remains a key measure of the overall success of the reforms. The post Tinubu’s reforms push Nigeria’s foreign reserves to $54.13bn – City Boy Movement appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Mock accreditation: Only two voters turn up at polling centres in Enugu
item.description: By Chinedu Adonu The nationwide mock accreditation exercise recorded a poor turnout in most polling centres in Enugu State on Saturday, with as few as two voters accredited by the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) in some centres as of 12 noon. A correspondent who monitored the exercise observed that the low turnout could be attributed to poor public awareness, late arrival of Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) ad hoc staff and difficulties encountered by some voters in locating their designated polling units. The exercise also coincided with the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Enugu State. At polling centres in Igbariam, Idaw River and Obiagu, among others, INEC ad hoc staff were observed arriving between 9:30 a.m. and 10 a.m., raising concerns about the late commencement of the exercise. Speaking at the Obiagu polling centre, a community leader, who identified himself simply as Mr Friday, attributed the poor turnout partly to the presidential visit. He said many residents had left their homes to receive President Tinubu at Okpara Square. According to him, those who turned out to welcome the President cut across party lines, as members of the APC and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), under the Rainbow Coalition, trooped out in large numbers. “So, it is clear that very few voters are currently around for the exercise, and most are not even aware or mobilised by local political leaders to participate,” he said. Also speaking, a resident of Achara Layout, Mr Arinze Madu, said he had visited two designated polling centres in search of his polling unit but had yet to locate his name. “There is little awareness to enable people know the designated polling units for the exercise in this Registration Area (RA), which is also a ward,” Madu said. Efforts to reach INEC’s Resident Electoral Commissioner in Enugu State, Dr Chukwuemeka Chukwu, for comments on the poor turnout and late arrival of electoral officials were unsuccessful, as calls to his mobile phone were not answered. The post Mock accreditation: Only two voters turn up at polling centres in Enugu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Kodak’s ultra-cute Charmera keychain camera is on sale for just $30
item.description: Kodak’s retro Charmera comes in multiple colors and styles. | Photos: Andrew Liszewski / The Verge We wouldn’t normally recommend a bad camera, but we’ll make an exception for the Kodak Charmera . As my colleague Andrew Liszewski pointed out in his review , the tiny retro keychain camera takes pretty lackluster photos, yet it’s charming enough that he kept using it anyway. That makes it a great gift for anyone who loves cute gadgets, especially now that it’s on sale at Amazon and B&H Photo for an all-time low of $29.74 (about $5 off). Kodak Charmera Keychain Digital Camera Where to Buy: $34.99 $29.74 at Amazon $34.99 $29.74 at B&H Photo The Charmera is small enough to carry on your keys and comes in a blind box, so you won’t know which of the six retro designs or the rarer transparent version you’re getting until you open it. It’s a simple point-and-shoot with a tiny LCD screen, and its 1,440×1,080-pixel photos often look fuzzy and washed out. Some of the built-in effects can make the results more interesting, though. Liszewski had some fun with the black-and-white mode and found that the red, blue, yellow, and gray pixel filters could produce bolder two-tone images. Video and audio quality are poor, too, and you can’t adjust much to improve them. Still, for a $30 keychain, it offers a surprising amount to play with. The Charmera isn’t something you’d want to rely on for an important occasion, but it can be fun to experiment with. Liszewski found that even though most pictures weren’t worth keeping, he’d occasionally get one interesting enough to share. That makes it a fun stocking stuffer for someone who loves cute, unusual gadgets. Read our full Kodak Charmera impressions .
