item.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

The high cost of building on the moon has led to wide-ranging research on how to make use of the moon's most plentiful resource: the dusty regolith that covers its surface. Right now, lunar shipping runs about $544,000 per pound ($1.2 million per kilogram), so anything that astronauts can make on the moon using existing materials could help a lot. Scientists have already proposed using regolith for building 3D-printed bricks , solar arrays , and even as soil to grow potatoes . Now, a team of researchers from Purdue University in Indiana have developed an aerogel made from simulated regolith for insulating lunar habitats. New aerogels created by Purdue University researchers, made of cellulose and lunar regolith simulant, could pave the way for insulating materials made on the moon. (Image credit: Purdue University photo/John Underwood) "Sustaining a long-term presence on the moon will require us to rethink how we use local resources," Wei, professor in Purdue's James Tarpo Jr. and Margaret Tarpo Department of Chemistry, said in a Nov. 19 statement . NASA has said that it wants a long-term, sustainable moon base up and running by 2032, a goal it aims to achieve via its Artemis program . "Rather than relying on Earth to supply everything we need, we're exploring how materials already available on the moon, including waste generated by its inhabitants, could be upcycled into something essential for safe and livable habitats," Wei said. The aerogel that the Purdue researchers have been working on is a mix of fiber from cardboard waste, called cellulose, and a material that simulates regolith. They said that it could protect the people living in habitats from the moon's drastic temperature swings. "Imagine an aerogel as a high-tech thermos for a lunar base," Jacob Staker, a graduate researcher working on the study, said in the same statement. "Most of it consists of empty space that insulates the interior, helping it maintain the temperature of what's inside." The idea here is not to create the best aerogel possible, Wei said, but that "we're looking for the sweet spot where we can get the properties we need with the limited resources we have available" on the moon. The research was published in September in the journal ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering.

item.title: Navy links operational successes to troops’ physical fitness
item.description: ….CNS urges personnel to sustain discipline, readiness By Kingsley Omonobi The Chief of the Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Idi Abass, has attributed operational successes recorded by the Nigerian Navy in 2026 against oil theft, maritime crimes and other security threats to the high physical standards and fitness of its personnel. Abass said the successes recorded in Operation Delta Sentinel and other joint operations across the country underscored the importance of physical fitness, endurance and teamwork among naval personnel. He spoke on Saturday while addressing officers and ratings during the Nigerian Navy’s Fourth Quarter Route March at the Naval Base, Abuja. He was represented by the Director of Project Implementation and Monitoring, Rear Admiral ML Dahiru. The naval chief said personnel had disrupted illegal refining sites, recovered suspected stolen crude oil and denied criminal elements proceeds from their activities. He added that naval personnel had also rescued kidnapped victims, protected critical maritime infrastructure, secured waterways and participated in ongoing counter-terrorism and counter-insurgency operations against violent extremist groups. “Our operational successes this year, particularly in Operation Delta Sentinel and across joint theatres nationwide, demonstrate why physical standards matter. “Behind each of these results are personnel who can sustain long hours on duty, remain alert as fatigue sets in and work together when the pressure is greatest,” he said. Abass explained that the quarterly route march was designed to build collective endurance, improve the physical fitness of personnel and strengthen teamwork across naval commands and formations. According to him, the exercise reinforces the standard that every officer and rating must remain physically fit and ready to respond whenever duty calls. He said the exercise also supported his mission to build a highly motivated and professional naval force capable of safeguarding Nigeria’s maritime interests and contributing effectively to joint military operations. The CNS noted that physically fit personnel were better equipped to meet the demands of patrols, emergency responses and joint counter-terrorism and counter-insurgency operations. Commending the dedication and resilience of the personnel, Abass urged them to sustain the discipline, vigilance and teamwork demonstrated during the exercise in their daily assignments. “As the year draws to a close, I urge you to carry the same discipline, vigilance and teamwork you demonstrated today into every assignment. While the Route March is quarterly, readiness is a daily responsibility,” he said. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 28, 1967: Astronomers Jocelyn Bell and Antony Hewish disover the 1st pulsar with Little Green Men 1 signal
item.description: null On November 28, 1967, astronomers found the first pulsar. A pulsar is a super-dense star that rotates super fast. As the pulsar spins, it emits two beams of light in opposite directions. When astronomers look at a pulsar, it looks like a star that's flickering on and off at a steady, constant pace. The first pulsar was observed by Jocelyn Bell Burnell and Antony Hewish. They were looking at the constellation Vulpecula when they saw a star flickering with regular pulses separated by 1.33 seconds. At first they had no idea what it was, so they jokingly nicknamed the signal Little Green Men 1. After more pulsars were discovered, they were able to rule out aliens. This chart tracked the signal of the first pulsar ever discoverered on Nov. 28, 1967. (Image credit: Cambridge University Library/Wikipedia) Why it mattered Pulsars are naturally occurring phenomena, and they can be handy tools for astronomers . For example, some pulsars are extremely accurate clocks. Because pulsars rotate, their emission of beams of radiation is observed at regular intervals. Until Burnell's discovery, astronomers did not know if neutron stars existed, let alone if they could be observed. "Suddenly, it turned out that nature has provided an incredibly precise way to observe these objects, something that has led to many later advances," said Edward Witten, chairman of the selection committee for the Fundamental Physics Breakthrough Prize, which in 2018 was awarded to Burnell . Among other applications, the observation of pulsars are one of the best ways astronomers have for testing Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity. The spinning stars have also been used as a navigation tool for spacecraft moving out beyond low Earth orbit. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Apathy mars INEC mock accreditation exercise in Abia
item.description: …Voter alleges demand for N1m to participate By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Voter apathy marred the mock accreditation and result-upload exercise conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Abia State on Saturday, with several polling units recording zero or minimal turnout. At Ibeku High School, one of the designated polling centres, Vanguard observed at about noon that no voter had turned up, while INEC officials waited for participants. A staff member of YIAGA Africa, who was monitoring the exercise, was also sighted at the centre but declined to comment. The situation was similar at School Road Primary School and Ugba Primary School, where electoral officials were on ground but voters were absent. Voters fault poor publicity, limited coverage At St. Stephen’s Primary School, Umuahia, however, some residents who turned out expressed disappointment that the exercise was restricted to selected polling units, blaming inadequate publicity for the low participation. Chimwe Kanu, a public servant, said she was excited about participating until she discovered that her polling unit was not among those selected for the exercise. “I’m happy to be here and to do the needful, but coming here, nothing is really happening because I was unable to vote or be captured. My polling unit is not part of the polling units selected. “I’m very disappointed because the happiness I came with, I didn’t see it again,” she said. Kanu said many prospective participants left after discovering that the exercise was limited to designated polling units. She urged INEC to improve its preparations for the 2027 general elections, particularly by ensuring the timely distribution of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs). “Many don’t have their voters’ cards. Their names are here, but their voters’ cards have not been given to them. They should make sure they share the voters’ cards as soon as possible. People need their voters’ cards,” she said. She also called on the commission to ensure early arrival of election officials and seamless accreditation of eligible voters, expressing hope that it would conduct credible elections in 2027. Similarly, Mike Uche criticised the publicity for the exercise, saying many residents arrived at polling centres unaware that participation was restricted to designated units. He said inadequate sensitisation left many confused and frustrated, alleging that some prospective participants demanded financial inducements before agreeing to take part in the exercise. Uche urged INEC to intensify voter education through radio announcements, community outreach and street sensitisation to improve participation and enlighten the electorate on the purpose of such exercises. “People are eager to come out and do the mock accreditation. They didn’t give the proper publicity,” he said, adding that participation should not be reduced to financial demands. item.title: Low turnout mars INEC mock accreditation exercise in Katsina
item.description: By Fauziyya Lawal, Katsina Low voter turnout and inadequate public awareness characterised the mock accreditation exercise conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Katsina State on Saturday ahead of the 2027 general elections. Vanguard monitoring of the exercise at Star Election Polling Unit, Wakilin Kudu 1, Kofar Gidan Iro Isansi, Rafin Dadi, showed that only a few voters turned out to participate, although some were successfully accredited. The low participation raised concerns about the level of public sensitisation and awareness among eligible voters regarding the importance of the exercise. The mock accreditation exercise is designed to test the functionality of the accreditation system, assess the preparedness of electoral officials and identify possible technical and operational challenges ahead of the actual elections. At the polling unit, the participation of the few voters provided an opportunity to observe the practical application of the accreditation process and assess the readiness of electoral personnel. The development also highlighted the need for increased public enlightenment to ensure that eligible voters understand the purpose and significance of such exercises. Adequate sensitisation is considered essential to encouraging participation in mock exercises, which enable electoral authorities to test arrangements and address possible challenges before the main elections. The exercise also provides an opportunity to identify operational gaps and resolve potential difficulties that could affect the smooth conduct of the 2027 general elections. INEC is expected to strengthen public enlightenment and stakeholder engagement to improve awareness and encourage greater voter participation in subsequent electoral exercises. The post Low turnout mars INEC mock accreditation exercise in Katsina appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Low turnout mars INEC mock accreditation in Lagos
item.description: Voters blame poor publicity for low participation By Olayinka Ajayi Low turnout of eligible voters marred the mock accreditation exercise conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in parts of Lagos State on Saturday, with some voters blaming the commission’s inadequate publicity. Polling agents expressed concern over the poor participation when Vanguard visited some of the designated polling units in Ijegun, Satellite Town and Festac, in the Amuwo-Odofin area of the state. An INEC polling agent at one of the polling units said only about 40 of the 250 registered voters had participated in the exercise as of the time of the visit. “The turnout has not been encouraging here. So far, about 40 people had voted out of 250 registered voters, and the BVAS has been cooperating smoothly due to good network. So we are certain of uploading the results after the exercise,” the agent said. A chieftain of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Festac, Mr Olusegun Samuel, attributed the low turnout to inadequate awareness among residents. He alleged that many eligible voters were unaware that the mock accreditation exercise was taking place. “Apart from the ruling APC, many people are not even aware that mock accreditation took place today. “INEC is encouraging voter apathy by not engaging in active publicity. By this, the ruling party would still have its way come the 2027 general elections,” he said. However, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Saheed Bakare, described the exercise as encouraging, despite the challenges and low turnout. He said INEC officials arrived at the polling unit around 9 a.m. and met some voters waiting to participate. “So far, so good. The exercise is not perfect but encouraging. INEC polling agent came around 9 a.m. and met voters on ground waiting for them. “Although we noticed poor turnout, maybe because of poor publicity, but on our own side as a party, we tried to sensitise our people too,” he said. Bakare described the exercise as an opportunity to assess his party’s level of preparedness ahead of the 2027 general elections. The post 2027: Low turnout mars INEC mock accreditation in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Dangote Refinery set to list on NGX December 1
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals FZE is scheduled to list 125,458,915,901 ordinary shares at N525 per share on the Main Board of Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) on Tuesday, 1 December 2026. The listing is expected to add approximately N65.87 trillion to the market capitalisation of NGX. The listing follows the company’s Initial Public Offering (IPO), which attracted approximately 3.8 million subscribers from 121 countries, including all 54 African countries, reflecting unprecedented investor participation in a Nigerian public equity offering. With a minimum subscription of N5,250 for 10 ordinary shares, the offer enabled investors across income groups and geographical locations to participate in the ownership of one of Africa’s largest industrial enterprises. Speaking at the launch of the IPO in September, Aliko Dangote, President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, described the offer as an opportunity to broaden public ownership and enable more Nigerians and Africans to participate in industrial wealth creation. “The Dangote refinery IPO is more than an investment opportunity; it is an opportunity for millions of Nigerians and Africans to build lasting wealth through ownership of a world-class industrial asset,” Dangote said. Investor participation at this scale was facilitated by NGX Invest, the SEC-approved digital capital-raising platform launched by Nigerian Exchange Group Plc (NGX Group) in June 2024. By enabling a network of 186 distribution channels, including stockbrokers, banks, fintech platforms and WhatsApp, NGX Invest provided the rail that significantly broadened access to the public offer. Temi Popoola, Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NGX Group, said: “The listing of Dangote Petroleum Refinery will mark an important milestone for Nigeria’s capital market, demonstrating its capacity to support large-scale industrial enterprises and mobilise long-term capital. The breadth of investor participation in the public offer also reflects the progress we have made in expanding market access. Through technology, strategic partnerships and a diverse distribution network, we are connecting more people to investment opportunities and more businesses to capital.” According to the company’s prospectus, net proceeds from the IPO will partly finance an estimated US$14.3 billion expansion programme designed to double refining capacity from 700,000 to approximately 1.4 million barrels per day. The transaction underscores the capital market’s strategic role in financing industrial expansion, broadening economic participation and supporting Nigeria’s ambition of becoming a US$1 trillion economy. Government officials, regulators, business leaders, market operators and representatives of African exchanges are expected to attend the listing ceremony. The post Dangote Refinery set to list on NGX December 1 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: INEC, security agencies addressing security concerns ahead of 2027 polls – Amupitan
item.description: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, says the commission, in collaboration with security agencies, is taking necessary steps to address all security concerns ahead of the 2027 general elections. Amupitan ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​⁠‌‌‍‍‌‌​stated this on Saturday in Jos while speaking with newsmen during the monitoring of the ongoing mock accreditation. Addressing a question on the security challenge and the likely implications on voter participation, Amupitan said the safety of ad hoc staff and all Nigerians remained a priority to the commission. “As the chairman of INEC, I’m also worried about the state of security in Nigeria, but you can see we are taking some good steps to ensure that we nip it in the bud. “Just two days ago, we had a national security conference where we brought together all the members of the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES), the police, the military, the Civil Defence, and other paramilitary agencies. “So, we had a one-day conference where we discussed all these issues,” he said. Amupitan said that INEC had conducted a risk assessment of every part of Nigeria, using Election Risk Management (ERM) tools. “We have identified all the polling units that are vulnerable, and we have shared this with the law enforcement agencies so that they can make extraordinary preparation for those places. “Any polling unit 500 meters from those vulnerable areas has been identified, and we are going to deal with it,” he said. Amupitan said the commission was interested in the security of the voters and ad hoc staff, particularly corps members. “It’s not every security matter you can bring to the open, but we are doing everything, both intelligence and physical, to ensure that the security on election day is assured,” he said. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the monitoring of the mock accreditation exercise was still ongoing in different parts of the state as of the time of filling this report. (NAN) The post INEC, security agencies addressing security concerns ahead of 2027 polls – Amupitan appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Electricity’ll improve, Mbah and I are working on Eastern Gas Pipeline – Tinubu
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has said electricity supply will improve in the South-East, adding that his administration has approved the Eastern Gas Pipeline and Eastern Nigeria rail line as part of plans to boost infrastructure and connectivity in the region. Tinubu made the remarks on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Enugu, where he said he was working with Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah on the gas pipeline project. “Electricity will improve. The Eastern Gas Pipeline is approved. Peter Mbah and I are working on it,” the president said. He also announced the approval of the Eastern Nigeria rail line, saying the projects would improve connections between the South-East, South-South and northern parts of the country. “Also approved is the Eastern Nigeria rail line. We will connect you, connect the East, South and North. It’s our honest promise for development,” he said. Addressing farmers in the region, Tinubu promised interest-free loans and financial support, alongside measures to reduce the challenges associated with farming. “To our farmers, they will receive money, loans that are interest-free. We will relieve them of the burdens of farming. We will connect with infrastructure,” he said. The president also urged residents to participate in the January 16 election, asking them to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and turn out to vote for the APC. “January 16, you must go out and vote. Take your friends, take your brothers, take your sisters. You must collect your PVC and go there, for President, vote APC, for honourable, APC,” Tinubu said. item.title: 2027: Adebayo pledges poverty-free Nigeria, justice, security
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Prince Adewole Adebayo, has promised to tackle poverty, insecurity, unemployment and other socio-economic challenges confronting Nigeria if elected in the 2027 general election. He also pledged to prioritise justice, free and quality education, affordable living costs and improved welfare for Nigerians. Adebayo spoke during a visit to the Emir of Lafia, His Royal Highness, Justice Sidi Dauda Bage Muhammad I (Rtd.), in Nasarawa State, where he presented the SDP’s vision and sought the monarch’s blessings ahead of the 2027 elections. The presidential candidate, who was accompanied by the SDP governorship candidate in Nasarawa State and former Inspector-General of Police, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, described the visit as particularly significant, noting that his relationship with the monarch went beyond politics. He said: “I am exceptionally happy today that, in all our appearances in this palace, this is the happiest because we came here with your son, IGP Abubakar Adamu.” Describing the Emir as a father, mentor and pillar of justice, Adebayo recalled his longstanding relationship with the monarch, dating back to his early years as a legal practitioner. He explained that the Emir had maintained a close relationship with his late uncle, who was the monarch’s friend during their days at law school. “His Highness is an uncle to me because he replaced my late uncle, who had been his friend since they were together in law school,” he said. Adebayo also recalled his professional encounters with Justice Bage, saying the monarch helped shape his understanding of courtroom practice when he appeared before him as a young lawyer. He recounted an incident during his first appearance before the monarch, when he was using what he described as his own style of English in court. “In my first appearance before His Lordship, I was appearing before Prince Adetokunbo Kayode, SAN. It was a very testy case, and I was using the language of my own English. His Lordship said, ‘We have our own language in this court.’ That is the language I have been using since that time,” he said. On the SDP’s choice of Adamu as its governorship candidate in Nasarawa, Adebayo described the former police chief as a distinguished professional whose experience in national and international policing would be valuable in addressing the state’s security challenges. He noted that Adamu’s service as a former Inspector-General of Police and Deputy Head of INTERPOL had strengthened the party’s confidence in his leadership capacity. “With Abubakar Adamu with us, we do not need to campaign because he is a professional of the highest distinction. He rose to the highest rank in the Nigerian Police and attained a high position in international policing as Deputy Head of INTERPOL,” he said. Adebayo expressed confidence that Adamu’s experience and ability to connect with ordinary Nigerians would attract support for the party

item.title: Referee faces suspension after punching goalkeeper in post-match rawl
item.description: A Bolivian referee, Jordy Aleman, might face be faced with strict suspension rules after punching Real Potosi goalkeeper Cristian Martinez during a post-match confrontation following the 2026 Copa Bolivia final. The incident occurred on Wednesday after Always Ready secured the trophy with a 3-1 aggregate victory over Real Potosi. The second leg ended in a goalless draw at the Victor Agustin Ugarte Stadium in Potosi. Tensions flared after the final whistle as Real Potosi players approached Aleman to protest decisions made during the match. Television footage showed the referee punching Martinez in the face, triggering further disorder before police intervened to protect the officials. Reports from Spanish-language media, including MARCA, said the confrontation followed an insult directed at Aleman by the goalkeeper. Martinez reportedly told the referee, “I hope your mother dies.” Martinez later said the punch left his mouth bleeding. However, in a defiant response reported by El Diario, he remarked: “He should hit harder.” The goalkeeper also questioned Aleman’s professionalism and called for an exemplary punishment. He subsequently announced that he would not pursue legal action or file a formal complaint over the incident. In a statement shared by Spanish publication 20 Minutos, Martinez said: “My intention is to consider this episode over and avoid allowing this situation to continue generating conflict.” Aleman could face disciplinary sanctions under the Bolivian Football Federation’s Disciplinary Code, which reportedly provides for fines of at least 20 national minimum monthly salaries and bans of between one and three years for physical assaults. The incident also led to four Real Potosi players and three members of the club’s coaching staff reportedly receiving red cards. According to Bolivian publication Vision 360, the federation’s refereeing authorities are expected to review the incident alongside the match reports. Aleman’s status as an international referee could also have further implications. The referee has yet to make a public statement on the incident. Rebecca Oladipo “I’m here at Narayi Primary School, one of the wards chosen for the mock exercise. I have been here for the past two hours. INEC is supposed to start the exercise at 8:30. item.title: Space in Macy’s 100 Thanksgiving Day parades
item.description: null The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is sure to be a blast, but it is a bit light on "space." According to previews provided by the department store chain, the founder of the New York City holiday celebration, space fans turning up or tuning in to catch sight of an astronaut or other nod to NASA will have only a returning rocket to look forward to on Saturday (Nov. 28). (The parade has been postponed two days from Thursday, Nov. 26, due to bad weather.) Not that Macy's (or the space agency) has hinted about anything cosmic planned for the 100th parade; it's only that the event has had a long history of celebrating space exploration with its floats and balloons. "For our 100th parade, we're creating a celebration of unprecedented scale and will deliver an unforgettable Thanksgiving for millions across the country," said Sharon Otterman, Macy's chief marketing officer, in a statement . First held in 1924 for Macy's colleagues, their friends and families, the Thanksgiving Day Parade has been held every year with the exception of a three-year break during World War II. Spanning longer than the dawn of the Space Age, the space race and NASA's entire 68-year history, the celebration has integrated space themes into its displays, even before the first rocket flew beyond Earth's atmosphere . Weighty weightless man The earliest space-themed feature of the parade may have been the "Space Ship," a float that made its first appearance in the 19th procession in 1945 and in various configurations — with and without astronauts and planets — appeared on and off through 1962. Perhaps more memorable, though, and certainly much larger, was the "Spaceman" (or, more appropriately, "The Giant Spaceman"). The 70-foot-long (21-meter) helium balloon made its debut in 1952, nine years before the Soviet Union's Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space. Described by Macy's as an "artist's conception of a visitor from another planet," the humanoid figure had a black spacesuit , a silver helmet and boots, a jet propulsion backpack and a black rocket gun. Once the heaviest balloon in the parade, the "Spaceman" was created by the Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company years before anyone had entered space. (Image credit: Macy's) Ironically, for a figure garbed for the weightless environment of space, the Spaceman was for a long time the parade's heaviest giant balloon. At 600 pounds (272 kilograms), it was only tied by the Pink Panther in 1988 and then exceeded two years later by Bart Simpson. The rubber Spaceman was created by Goodyear Tire, the same company that contributed hardware to NASA's Apollo program , including the wire mesh non-pneumatic tires for the lunar roving vehicle. The Spaceman survived being torn when it was caught with a lamppost in 1955, and a helium shortage resulting in it and other balloons being filled with air and held up by cranes in 1958. It was retired after its seventh appearance in 1959, and ultimately was destroyed. 'The First Men on the

item.title: PHOTOS: Low Turnout as INEC begins Mock Election
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) commenced its mock elections in Borno State to test-run voting equipment and logistical readiness ahead of the 2027 general elections. However, the exercise recorded a low voter turnout in some polling units visited by our correspondent due to what many residents described as “a lack of awareness”. The exercise, designed to evaluate the deployment of election personnel and the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) across all 27 local government areas of the state, also faced a slow start in some polling units. Across Jere and Maiduguri Metropolitan Councils security personnel, including police officers and the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and Road Safety Officials, were present early at some polling units, INEC officials arrived late. Yul recalls Pete Edochie’s final moments 3 killed, many injured as rival youth groups clash in Cross River At the Bulama Jidda polling unit in Gomari Airport, voting commenced at 8:44 a.m. after officials arrived, slightly behind schedule. However, poll workers and voters at the station confirmed that the BVAS machines functioned efficiently. “There is actually a low turnout, but the use of BVAS is smooth. At some point, we are using it offline, but will upload it when we reach areas with a robust network,” one polling unit officer stated. Interviews with residents across various areas revealed that public awareness of the exercise was generally poor, with many locals unaware that the mock election was taking place. At the Gwange III polling unit, turnout was similarly low. Some prospective voters said they encountered some technical hitches during accreditation, reporting that the BVAS failed to capture their fingerprints and facial features. Speaking on condition of anonymity, an Ad-hoc staff, noted that affected individuals were not issued ballot papers. Instead, their details were compiled for INEC to review and resolve prior to the general elections. At the Government House polling unit (Unit 001, Maisandari Ward), where voter turnout was notably impressive, the process ran without hitches. Abacha Anas, the Electoral Officer for Operations for INEC in the Maiduguri Metropolitan Council, described the exercise as smooth and successful.

item.title: 2026 Kindle Paperwhite review: Page-turn buttons are back, for a price
item.description: Supply pressures, shortages, and inflation have pushed tech prices relentlessly upward over the last half-decade, and even basic gadgets haven't been immune. That's why you can spend $385 on a Raspberry Pi, or why the cheapest Amazon Kindle in 2026 costs more than the midrange one from a few years ago . "New thing, better features, same price" used to be a reliable formula, but now you're lucky if you can get the same thing for barely more than before. The 2024 Kindles all came with small price increases, but the 2026 models make them look like stellar deals. The $160 Kindle Paperwhite from two years ago wipes the floor with this year's $150 Kindle in just about every conceivable way, from screen size to front light quality to waterproofing—something to consider if you're choosing between a used or refurbished Paperwhite and one of these new models. The flagship of the now five-model-large monochrome Kindle family is the $250 2026 Paperwhite Signature Edition, which takes the core specs of the new $200 Paperwhite and puts it in a sturdy iPad-esque aluminum case instead of the typical plastic. item.title: INEC Declares Readiness For 2027, Expresses Satisfaction With Plateau Mock Election
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has declared its readiness for the 2027 general elections, assuring Nigerians that it is committed to conducting free, inclusive, credible and transparent polls. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, gave the assurance while monitoring Saturday’s mock election in Plateau State, where he expressed satisfaction with the turnout of voters and the conduct of the exercise. Amupitan said the mock election was designed to test the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), as well as assess the efficiency of the accreditation process ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC Chairman Amupitan inspecting the exercise in Jos on Saturday, November 28, 2026. He commended voters for their orderly conduct, expressing delight at seeing an elderly woman turn out for the exercise and successfully undergo accreditation. “You can see yourself that the turnout is very good. What we are trying to test is actually the working of the machines, which are the BVAS and the IReV, and voters are being accredited. You can see how orderly it is going. From what we have seen, I am impressed,” he said. The INEC chairman acknowledged the support of the Plateau State Independent Electoral Commission in mobilising residents for the exercise but noted that the environmental sanitation exercise earlier scheduled for Saturday may have affected early participation, as some residents had indicated they would be unable to come out in time. On the commission’s preparedness for the 2027 elections, Amupitan said INEC was determined to deliver one of the best elections in the country’s history. “For the 2027 general elections, INEC is prepared, and I want to assure all Nigerians that we are going to have one of the best elections. We are determined that the 2027 election will be free, inclusive, credible and transparent,” he stated. Addressing concerns over the security situation in the country, the INEC chairman said the commission was working with relevant security agencies to ensure the protection of voters and electoral personnel during the forthcoming elections. He disclosed that INEC recently convened a one-day national security conference where stakeholders deliberated on security challenges and measures to safeguard the electoral process. INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, seen addressing staff and voters in Jos on Saturday, NOVEMBER 28, 2026. Amupitan further revealed that the commission had conducted a risk assessment of polling units across the country, with identified locations shared with law enforcement agencies to enable them to strengthen security arrangements ahead of the elections. “We have done what we call a risk assessment of all the polling units in Nigeria, and we have identified all the polling units and shared them with the law enforcement agencies so that they can make extra preparations ahead of the elections,” he said. item.title: Numbers ‘Impressive’ As Voters Turnout For INEC Mock Exercise In Kano
item.description: The mock accreditation for the 2027 general elections is underway in Paniso ward, Kano, as voters were seen turning out in seemingly impressive numbers for the exercise, compared to other regions in the country. Our correspondent, who monitored one of the selected polling units, noted that two INEC staff and two ad hoc personnel are testing the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices. Although voter turnout is still relatively low as against what is expected, the exercise is progressing smoothly, with no discrepancies reported and the BVAS thumbprint verification functioning as expected so far. Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Joash Amupitan, is currently in Jos to inspect the ongoing mock accreditation exercise, ahead of the 2027 general elections. It’s about seven weeks before the 2027 general election, and INEC is today running a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Professor Joash Amupitan, INEC Chairman, disclosed this at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday. According to him, the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) validation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. The presidential and National Assembly elections hold on 16 January 2027 across 177,299 polling units, with governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections to follow on 6 February 2027. item.title: 12 grains of dust found high in Earth's atmosphere reveal secrets of water at the edge of the solar system
item.description: A dozen grains of dust that have wandered in from the distant Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune were found floating in Earth's stratosphere. And it turns out they hold the secrets of a special kind of 'heavy' water that seems to be surprisingly abundant in the outer solar system. When analyzed by a team of scientists the 12 dust grains, which were captured by NASA's stratospheric ER-2 research aircraft, show signs of having interacted with a form of water that contains heavy oxygen isotopes. This is important because to better understand how the planets formed, scientists are seeking to understand how various materials were distributed around the early solar system 4.5 billion years ago. If there is a reservoir of heavy water out in the solar system's hinterlands, understanding how that water got out there and stayed out there will inform models that describe the growth of the planets. Water consists of two hydrogen atoms and an oxygen atom. What we usually refer to as heavy water is water that contains a heavy isotope of hydrogen. An isotope is an atom that contains the usual number of protons for that element, but a different number of neutrons . Elements are determined by the number of protons they contain. For example, hydrogen always has just one proton. Ordinary 'light' hydrogen has 1 proton and no neutrons, but its heavy isotopes – deuterium and tritium – contain 1 and 2 neutrons, respectively, in addition to the proton. However, there's another kind of water that features heavy isotopes of oxygen instead. Ordinary 'light' oxygen is made from 8 protons and 8 neutrons and is hence known as oxygen-16 but some oxygen isotopes can have 9 or 10 neutrons, and we call these isotopes oxygen-17 or -18. There have been a few clues that such a reservoir exists. Mineralogical evidence from a single carbonaceous chondritic meteorite and measurements from comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko indicated the presence of minerals that had formed from interactions between silicate rock and abundant oxygen-heavy variety of water, but it was not clear whether these were isolated instances or a clue to something more widespread. An illustration comparing the locations of the solar system planets to the Kuiper Belt and the Oort Cloud, a theorized shell of icy objects at the farthest reaches of our solar system. (Image credit: ESA) Another data point comes from NASA's Genesis mission, which launched in 2001 and collected particles from the solar wind that were subsequently returned to Earth for study. The analysis of these particles indicated that the sun contains proportionally more ordinary 'light' oxygen than Earth and most meteorites. This suggests that there could be an outwards gradient of increasing abundance of heavy oxygen. Yet the Kuiper Belt is so far away that it makes finding more evidence for this difficult. However, rather than having to go to the Kuiper Belt to sample the water-ice there, dust grains can bring a little bit of the Kuiper Belt to us. T

item.title: Quantum: 'Five years, that's all we got…'
item.description: SC26 in Chicago had the usual quantum booths, discussions, and hallway optimism. A lot of people were talking about integration with classical HPC and Slurm scheduling for quantum processors, co-design platforms, and GPU-accelerated error correction tools. That part is real and useful. What was harder to find was any result that changed the basic math on when quantum systems will actually do something a supercomputer can't already handle better. I had a long conversation in St. Louis (SC25) with a contact who works deep in quantum and has spent decades in HPC. He's not a skeptic for sport, although that can be fun, sure. Over a grifted free dinner in Chicago (the best kind), his take this year remains the same: the hype keeps outrunning the error rates. Quantum computers generate too many errors to give usable answers on anything interesting. Fixing that is the whole game. And that's a five-year game, minimum. Much like the Bowie anthem in the title. Qubits by the numbers There are two kinds of qubits. Physical qubits are the actual hardware: ions, superconducting circuits, and atoms in a trap. Logical qubits are the ones that do the computation. Each logical qubit is built out of many physical ones so the system can detect and correct errors while it runs. With the traditional surface-code approach, one logical qubit often needs somewhere between 500 and 2,000 physical qubits backing it up, depending on the hardware and the code. One logical qubit by itself is useless. Estimates for basic scientific modeling and small-scale simulation sit in the 100-to-500 logical-qubit range. Take the midpoint of 300. At the low end of the overhead that is 150,000 physical qubits. At the high end it is several million. That is only for early science. Commercial work like molecular mapping for pharma, large optimization problems, complex financial models, pushes into the thousands of logical qubits. National-security and encryption-related work sits even higher. Those numbers have not magically shrunk. A system that can map a modestly sized drug molecule, or run a materials simulation that is still too slow on classical machines, is the kind of workload people actually mean when they talk about useful quantum advantage. Until the logical-qubit counts get there with error rates low enough to finish the job, those problems stay on the machines we already know how to build. Ok, so let's just scale it up This is the world of HPC, we know how to scale stuff, right? Yes, but this isn't a matter of adding a few more racks. Scaling to an additional few hundred thousand physical qubits is not a rack or two or ten. It's probably a dedicated building with its own cryogenics, control electronics, and power draw that is still measured in megawatts even before you get useful logical capacity. This is why cutting the massive gap between logical and physical qubits is critical if quantum is going to become even narrowly useful. Signs of (incremental) improvement There is a newe

item.title: Unkernel and Trynix just transported computing to 2035
item.description: What's the difference between just-for-fun demo hacks, and serious carefully designed large-scale software architecture? It's the quick-and-dirty jobs that end up transforming computing. A blog post earlier this week called 2035 came early led the Reg FOSS desk down what we thought was a fascinating, and possibly quite scary, rabbit-hole… but it turned out to be an entire warren. We thought we were still in 2026, but in turns out that in some ways, tech just leaped forward a decade. To try to convey the point of this blog post – why what had been just a fun clever little hack has the potential to take half a century of OS and hypervisor design and throw it out of the nearest window – will take quite a lot of unpacking. If you bear with us, we will try to walk you through it. To get started, we need to go back a decade or more. Stick with this: there are laughs, as well as hammers taken to beloved ideas. The year of 2035 and the ideas around that come from a remarkable talk by Gary Bernhardt of Destroy All Software, which is both funny and highly educational. It will really massively assist understanding what this article and the technology is all about if you have the time to watch the talks. The Reg FOSS desk is not at all fond of spoken-word video as a medium – we much prefer to read than listen – but the three talks we're going to mention are golden, among the very best presentations this century in all of computing and IT. Seriously, they are worth your time. As a preface, before we go into Bernhardt's half-hour information-dense talk, let's warm up with a four-minute funny one. But first, let's look at the context for that. Step 0: JavaScript is the language of web programming In 2009, Jeff Atwood laid this out in an article called All Programming is Web Programming . It's still coming true today. Software is getting very blurred around the edges. The entire SaaS industry means that massive organizations run on web apps. Tech like Electron embeds a web browser inside JavaScript apps built in Node.js, while Progressive Web Apps make websites look like local program windows. The most popular desktop Linux in the world is ChromeOS Flex, which doesn't support local native applications at all. Everything is browser windows, even the desktop. It's all built in JavaScript. And yet… Step 1: JavaScript is kind of weird and kind of bad. Bernhardt made this case in 2012, with a celebrated lightning talk called Wat , from the CodeMash conference in 2012. Wat walks through a whole list of examples of how JavaScript is a very strange programming language and does very strange things that are not at all what you might expect. Some of the jokes will make more sense to programmers, but we reckon anyone who has ever fought with a recalcitrant bit of software will get some laughs from it – and that probably applies to all readers of The Register. Step 2: JavaScript is in the process of conquering the world. Bernhardt moved on to much bigger ideas at PyCon 2014

item.title: CHINA DIARIES: Where Students Build the Future
item.description: I must confess, I was not quite prepared for what I saw during my visit to the Qinling Workshop at Xi’an Aeronautical Vocational and Technical College in China. For someone fascinated by technology and innovation, walking into the institution’s aircraft hangar was an experience in itself. There were aircraft and helicopters, aviation equipment and specialised training facilities. For a moment, it felt less like visiting a school and more like stepping into an aviation engineering centre. But the biggest surprise was yet to come. Beyond the aircraft and helicopters, I encountered something that left an even stronger impression: drones designed, developed and assembled by students. China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents China Diaries: The future of farming These were not simply classroom models or academic projects put together to earn grades. The students were experimenting with different drone technologies, exploring their applications and developing solutions to practical problems. There were different designs and innovations, reflecting the creativity, technical confidence and curiosity of young people who were not waiting until graduation to start making a contribution to society. It was exciting to see. One could immediately imagine the possibilities: drones that could help farmers monitor crops and spray farmlands, support environmental monitoring, conduct aerial surveys, inspect infrastructure and assist emergency response operations. What struck me most was the philosophy behind what I was seeing. Technology was not being taught as an abstract subject. Students were being encouraged to understand problems and develop technological solutions. An institution built around practical skills The Qinling Workshop visit offered an opportunity to appreciate the work of Xi’an Aeronautical Vocational and Technical College, an institution with a strong focus on aviation, engineering and technical education. Its programmes cover a wide range of disciplines, including aviation manufacturing, aircraft maintenance, aircraft engine technology, drone application technology, general aviation, mechanical engineering, artificial intelligence, computer technology, robotics, automation, electronic information, aviation logistics and automotive technology. Students also study specialised areas such as CNC machining, intelligent manufacturing, aircraft electronic systems, materials engineering, welding technology, surveying and remote sensing, software development, big data, airport operations and civil aviation services. The breadth of these programmes is significant. It shows an understanding that an aviation and manufacturing economy requires much more than pilots and aircraft engineers. It needs technicians, software developers, mechanics, materials specialists, electronics experts, maintenance professionals and people who can design, manufacture and repair equipment. item.title: The M5 MacBook Air just got its biggest discount since Apple raised the price
item.description: The M5-powered MacBook Air is $300 off in both size configurations for Black Friday. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge If you’ve been holding off on buying a new MacBook Air since Apple raised prices by $200 in June , you’re in luck. The 13-inch M5 MacBook Air is on sale at Amazon and Best Buy with 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage starting at $999 ($300 off) for Black Friday, which is the lowest price we’ve seen since the hike. If you want a larger display, Amazon and Best Buy are also taking $300 off the otherwise identical 15-inch model with 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage, dropping it to $1,199. Apple MacBook Air 13 (M5) Where to Buy: $1299 $999 at Amazon (512GB) $1299 $999 at Best Buy (512GB) $1599 $1199 at Amazon (1TB) Apple MacBook Air 15 (M5) Where to Buy: $1299 $1199 at Amazon (512GB) $1299 $1199 at Best Buy (512GB) $1799 $1499 at Amazon (1TB) The M5-equipped MacBook Air is a good middle ground if you need more power than the MacBook Neo — which, thanks to a $100 discount , is $599 — but don’t want to splurge on a MacBook Pro. Its faster chip, 16GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage make it better suited for multitasking and creative work in apps like Photoshop and Premiere. You also get a higher-resolution display, better speakers, a backlit keyboard that makes typing in the dark easier, and faster ports. Plus, its sharper webcam supports Apple’s Center Stage feature, which automatically adjusts the framing to keep you in view during video calls. Of course, the Air can’t match the performance or higher-end displays you can get with a MacBook Pro, whether you opt for an M5 model , the newer M5 Pro model with a PROLED XDR Display , or one of the M6-powered machines . A Pro may be worth the extra money if you regularly edit video or work on more demanding creative projects. But if you mostly need a laptop for work, browsing, and occasional photo or video editing, the M5 Air is more than capable. Read our M5-powered MacBook Air review .

item.title: Dropping missiles from orbit? 2 European companies sign agreement to study the idea
item.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration. Atmos and MBDA also said this work could lead to demonstrations, but the companies' announcement makes it clear that any deployment or use would be subject to the approval of governmental and military authorities. "The initiative also directly supports MBDA's broader strategic vision in the space domain, reinforcing both space for defense and the defense of space," Thomas Gottschild, MBDA Deutschland managing director, said in the same statement. This news comes a few months after Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess said that the U.S. Space Force operates orbital weapons . "Let me be crystal clear: Today, Guardians operate on-orbit weapons that can defend the joint force against space-enabled attacks," Schiess said during a conferenace presentation on Sept. 15 ("Guardians" refers to Space Force personnel.) Last year, Atmos' Phoenix capsule got its first test run in space. The cargo-return technology launched aboard a Space X Falcon 9 rocket during a rideshare mission in February 2025. Atmos tested out the inflatable heat shields it has been working on to help future space-manufactured cargo make it through Earth's atmosphere in one piece. "Orbital transportation and return form a new layer of strategic infrastructure, and infrastructure determines what Europe can achieve on its own terms," Klaus said in the Nov 18 statement.

item.title: Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack Binance has fully lifted the withdrawal suspension it put in place after last month’s record $6.3 billion hack, saying its recovery work is complete and that withdrawals are open across nearly all networks. “Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted,” the exchange said in an X post Thursday afternoon. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. Launderers turn to THORChain and coinjoin The unfrozen funds are on the move. North Korean launderers have stepped up transfers through THORChain and a coinjoin service in recent days, blockchain researchers told Reuters , as part of an operation spanning tens of thousands of transactions across blockchains. Chainalysis and Elliptic estimate that more than $600 million of the stolen crypto has passed through THORChain, though Elliptic said that figure could count funds that went through more than once. TRM Labs estimates THORChain earned as much as $1 million in fees from the swaps. Separately, $342 million has moved through a coinjoin service mostly coordinated by a pseudonymous figure named Kruw, Elliptic said. A coinjoin combines coins from many users into a single transaction, so their origin is no longer visible on the blockchain. item.title: Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. Ordinary investors still face tight limits once they pass. Non-qualified buyers can only purchase bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT, and no more than 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary. SPB Exchange sets Dec. 1 start Exchange trading is next. item.title: The best Black Friday deals Ars could find
item.description: Every year has a Prime Day—some years even have two Prime Days!—where we celebrate the life and achievements of the greatest leader the Autobots have ever known: the inimitable Optimus Prime. But just as every dawn is twinned by a dusk that steals its light, so too did Optimus Prime's bright spark fade, extinguished by the foul hand of Megatron during the Great Decepticon Incursion of 2005 . It is a day that lives in infamy forever, and we all know the tale—how the evil Megatron (cursed be the flow of his energon!) commandeered an Autobot shuttle, cruelly murdered its crew, and launched a cowardly surprise attack against Autobot City—a plan utterly bereft of honor, as was so typical of Megatron's schemes. Even as individual Autobots strove to secure Autobot City— heroes, all of them !—hope began to fade under an onslaught that included an attack by the fearsome Devastator , against which there appeared to be no defense. And then, at the precipice of disaster, Optimus Prime made the fateful declaration whose words still ring out to this day: " Megatron must be stopped, no matter the cost ." The fearless Autobot transformed, rolled out, and got the job done—even though that cost was high. Many brave Autobots besides Optimus Prime lost their lives during the fighting. It was truly a dark day, a black day—and so, every year on the Friday after Thanksgiving, we pause to remember the noble sacrifices made by Prime and by so many others. This is why today is known as Black Friday. Read full article Comments

item.title: Who turned the W upside down? Why Cassiopeia won't sit still
item.description: null Some constellations are like old friends. You know them well, they're always there, and they never seem to change. A case in point is Cassiopeia, the queen. Its beautiful name comes from Greek mythology — the mother of Andromeda — and its shape is said to represent a queen sitting on a throne. To a stargazer, Cassiopeia is best known as a prominent northern constellation shaped like the letter W. It's easy to find — look north, find five reasonably bright stars making a W, congratulate yourself on finding Cassiopeia and use it to get somewhere more interesting. It's so often a signpost, not a destination. But look north a few hours after dark this month, and you'll notice the W has gone. The five stars are still there, but the shape you may have memorized looks like it's been picked up and turned over. It looks more like an E or an M, depending on when you look. Now try and look for the Big Dipper /the Plough. It's gone. Nothing mysterious has happened, of course. Cassiopeia is doing exactly what it always does, but it's a reminder that the northern sky is where you can easily watch the stars move — and the seasons turn. What's happening and when to look Stars move anti-clockwise around the north celestial pole, so Cassiopeia changes orientation. (Image credit: Alan Dyer/Stocktrek Images via Getty Images) Late November is an excellent time to reacquaint yourself with Cassiopeia from anywhere in the Northern Hemisphere. Look high in the northern sky during the evening for its five prominent stars — Caph, Schedar, Navi, Ruchbah and Segin. Depending on exactly when you look, it can look like a W, E, M or a 3. This is because Cassiopeia is circumpolar. Rather than rising in the east and eventually setting in the west like many familiar constellations , it circles the north celestial pole — a position currently held by Polaris , the North Star. From sufficiently northerly latitudes, its main stars never disappear below the horizon. This gives us a simple observing experiment. Find Cassiopeia in the early evening and remember its orientation relative to the horizon. Go back several hours later and look again. The constellation has moved around Polaris, and its shape has changed. The stars haven't changed their arrangement — Earth has simply rotated from west to east. We all know this logically, but watching the familiar pattern of Cassiopeia's stars apparently tip over during a single night makes Earth's rotation a lot less abstract. How and when I'm watching it The names and distances of the stars in Cassiopeia. (Image credit: Starry Night) I'm going to observe Cassiopeia twice on the same evening this week, which is about as complicated as the experiment needs to get. The first time will be shortly after darkness falls. I'll find the W, note which way it seems to be pointing and use something fixed — a rooftop, tree or chimney — to give myself a rough reference for its position. I'll return to my backyard before bed, and see where the pattern ha

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 27, 1885: Astronomer captures 1st known photo of a meteor during an Andromedid meteor storm
item.description: null On Nov. 27, 1885, an astronomer made the first known photograph of a meteor. The picture was taken by Austro-Hungarian astronomer Ladislaus Weinek. He captured the trail of the meteor on a photographic plate in the Czech Republic. The meteor he captured was part of the Andromedid meteor shower . The Andromedids were associated with Biela's Comet , which broke apart in the 1850s. When Weinek observed the meteor shower in 1885, it was in the middle of a meteor storm . This means that there were way more meteors than usual. Skywatchers could see thousands of meteors per hour. The November 1872 incidence of the Andromedid meteor shower, as seen over France, in a painting. (Image credit: Alto Vintage Images/Alamy) Why it mattered Not many stargazers may be be acquainted with the Andromedid meteor shower. What used to be a spectacular annual meteor shower is now hardly even visible. But in 1885, the Andromedids were an annual treat for skywatchers hoping for a chance to see the remains of Biela's comet (a comet first spotted in 1772 and then found - for the third time - in 1826 by the German astronomer Wilhelm von Biela, from whom it gets its name). Meteor Shower Quiz: How Well Do You Know 'Shooting Stars'? This modern photo of the Geminid meteor shower shows dozens of meteors captured in a long exposure by Josh Drury. Ladislaus Weinek, who captured the first photo of a meteor, had to use a photographic plate in 1889. (Image credit: Josh Dury) Camera technology has come a long way since 1885, which is good since it is a bit harder to see the Andromedids these days. Instead of photographic plates or digital cameras, astronomers now have to use special tracking equipment to record images of Andromedid meteors. In 2011, astronomers announced that the meteor shower seemed to be undergoing a resurgence of activity, with 50 meteors per hour, and upticks were expected in 2018 and 2023. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. The Petions then launched NovaTech, falsely marketed it as a registered hedge fund broker and advertised trading profits of about 2% to 4% a week. Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. More than 11,000 New Yorkers invested, alongside what the state called hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide. NovaTech collapsed in May 2023, and tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their crypto. The state sued in June 2024. The Petions never answered the complaint. item.title: Smartphone shipments face another bleak year before modest 2028 comeback
item.description: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028. That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers. The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market. Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. "Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. The result is a much weaker 2027, particularly for lower priced devices and price sensitive markets." Global shipments are forecast to rebound by 6 percent in 2028, but that would bring shipments only roughly back to this year's already shrunken level, rather than hitting the peak of previous years. Counterpoint cautions that the scale of the rebound will depend on how quickly lower component costs translate into retail pricing. A speedy improvement in mobile memory allocation during the second half of 2027 could bring replacement demand forward and swell shipments, but continued competition from the AI market or another round of handset price increases would hinder recovery. item.title: Artemis III astronauts meet their spacecraft | Space photo of the day for Nov. 27, 2026
item.description: null NASA's Artemis III astronauts pose holding up three fingers to symbolize their mission as they visit the Orion spacecraft they will ride to space. (Image credit: NASA/Kim Shiflett) Training for a mission to space is hard work. But sometimes you have to take a minute and have a little fun with your crewmates. What is it? Crowded together with the Orion spacecraft, the four astronauts that make up the Artemis III crew hold up three fingers, taking a brief pause in their rigorous training for some lighthearted crew bonding. In the snapshot , the crew — from left to right, NASA astronauts Randy Bresnick (mission commander) and Frank Rubio (mission specialist), European Space Agency astronaut Luca Parmitano (mission pilot) and NASA astronaut Andre Douglas (mission specialist) — is spotted posing alongside the same Orion spacecraft that they will fly to space as part of their mission. This brief moment of levity took place where the spacecraft currently resides at the Neil A. Armstrong Operations and Checkout Building at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Why is it incredible? This crew has a serious mission ahead of them. The four astronauts will launch to low-Earth orbit around Earth where they plan to practice rendezvous and docking with both Blue Origin and SpaceX's lunar landing vehicles , Blue Moon and Starship, respectively. To prepare, the crew has to undergo months of critical training to both be physically ready while prepared to handle any situation that might come up during their mission. And while Artemis III isn't landing astronauts on the moon, it is a critical step toward that goal. If Artemis III goes to plan and NASA has a lunar landing vehicle that passes rendezvous and docking tests with the Orion spacecraft, Artemis IV might see astronauts land on the moon for the first time since the final Apollo mission in 1972.
